items.text: The controller shall run its supervisor software and its application software on one STMicroelectronics STM32N657X0 microcontroller.
items.rationale: Platform fact given by CON-SUP-001; the stakeholder context places supervisor and application on one microcontroller. Hardware facts of this device are taken only from RM0486 by document id, section and page in later stages.

items.text: The supervisor software shall be written in the C11 language.
The supervisor software shall use no dynamic memory allocation.
The supervisor software shall use no recursion.

The controller shall take the set of supervised tasks, the period, start limit and execution limit of each supervised task, and the checkpoint order of the control cycle from the configuration data block, so that changing them requires no change to the supervisor program code.
items.rationale: Terms used throughout this set: 'supervised task' is a task named in the configuration data block; 'control cycle' is the 10 ms period (CON-SUP-101); 'start limit' and 'execution limit' are the per-task timing limits of CON-SUP-103. Configured schedule (F-sys-req-set-r3-001): the configured schedule is the one release schedule that alive supervision (SYS-SUP-001), program-flow supervision (SYS-SUP-005) and the verifications that enumerate scheduled releases (SYS-TEST-011) use. For each supervised task it is the set of control cycles in which a release of that task is scheduled: every n-th control cycle, n being the configured period of the task divided by the 10 ms control cycle (CON-SUP-101), counted from the control cycle of the first release of that task after start-up (OP-SYS-020 (b)), with the releases of one control cycle in the release order of SYS-CFG-009 (OP-SYS-039). With the default configuration (SYS-CFG-002, SYS-CFG-003) it is the schedule of CON-SUP-101, which the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006 releases, so the supervised schedule and the application releases coincide. For a configured period that differs from the default, the inputs do not say which governs the application releases: STK-SUP-004 requires the timing of the supervised tasks to be set by configuration, while CON-SUP-006 gives the scheduler 10 ms and 100 ms periods. If the scheduler kept its own periods and only supervision used the configured period, supervision would expect releases in control cycles where none occurs (SYS-SUP-005 then detects a program-flow fault) or receive checkpoints of releases it does not expect. This item therefore does not state that a changed period changes the application releases. Whether the scheduler takes its release periods from the configuration data block, which periods are supported (CON-SUP-006 names only 10 ms and 100 ms; CON-SUP-115 rejects only a zero period), and whether a configured period that the scheduler does not release is a configuration-range fault, is recorded in OP-SYS-046 (blocking); this item stays open until it is decided.

items.text: The default configuration shall define the supervised tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT with a period of 10 ms each.
The default configuration shall define the supervised task T_DIAG with a period of 100 ms, released after T_OUT in every tenth control cycle.
The default configuration shall define the checkpoint order of each control cycle as T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, followed by T_DIAG in the control cycles in which T_DIAG is released.
In each control cycle, the controller shall release the supervised tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT of the default configuration in the order T_IN, then T_CTRL, then T_OUT.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r1-001. CON-SUP-101 fixes the release sequence of the three 10 ms tasks in each control cycle. SYS-CFG-002 gives only their periods and SYS-CFG-004 gives the checkpoint order, which an implementation could meet while releasing the tasks in another order; this item states the release sequence separately from the checkpoint order. The release of T_DIAG after T_OUT in every tenth control cycle is SYS-CFG-003 and is not repeated. STK-SUP-004 requires the order of the tasks to be set by configuration; whether the release order is a value of the configuration data block (in addition to the checkpoint order of SYS-CFG-001) or is fixed by the timer-driven scheduler of CON-SUP-006, and whether a configuration may set a release order that differs from the checkpoint order, is not given by the inputs and is recorded in OP-SYS-039; this item states the default sequence in either case. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with the default configuration and no fault injected, record on one time base the release event of every supervised task over at least 20 consecutive control cycles, including two releases of T_DIAG. Pass: in every recorded control cycle each of T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT is released exactly once, the release of T_IN is recorded before the release of T_CTRL, and the release of T_CTRL before the release of T_OUT, in the order of the event record. A cycle in which any of the three is missing, repeated or out of this order fails. Observation of releases: OP-SYS-037.

items.text: The default configuration shall set the start limit of every supervised task to 2 ms after its release.
The default configuration shall set the execution limit of each supervised task with a 10 ms period to 3 ms.
The default configuration shall set the execution limit of the supervised task T_DIAG to 20 ms.
items.rationale: The 20 ms value is the CON-SUP-103 default and is kept unchanged. The item states the configured limit only; it does not claim that the default schedule is feasible. With the defaults (CON-SUP-101, CON-SUP-103) the execution limits add up to 3 x 3 ms x 10 cycles + 20 ms = 110 ms of application execution per 100 ms on the single processor, before supervisor execution. The inputs give no workload evidence showing which execution times can occur together, so the schedulability of the configured schedule is not established; this is recorded in OP-SYS-013.

items.text: Before releasing any supervised task after a reset, the controller shall detect a configuration-range fault when the configuration data block contains a timing limit longer than the period of its task, a task period of zero, or a task identifier that is not in the approved set of supported task identifiers defined independently of the configuration data block.
items.rationale: Validity of the range check on a block whose integrity check has failed or not yet completed, and precedence over SYS-RST-012, are open in OP-SYS-040 (F-sys-req-set-r1-002). Covers exactly the out-of-range conditions listed in CON-SUP-115. The 'unknown task' condition of CON-SUP-115 is checked against an approved set of supported task identifiers, not against the supervised-task definition of SYS-CFG-001, because that definition is taken from the configuration data block under check and would accept any task entered into it. The inputs do not give the approved set: CON-SUP-101 names T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG as the supervised tasks, which SYS-CFG-002 and SYS-CFG-003 treat as the default configuration, while STK-SUP-004 lets the configuration select the supervised tasks; whether the approved set is exactly these four identifiers, and where it is fixed, is recorded in OP-SYS-014. Whether the CON-SUP-115 list is exhaustive is recorded in OP-SYS-011. The reaction (latched safe state) is SYS-RST-003.

items.text: Before releasing any application task after a reset, the controller shall check the integrity of the application program code image stored in flash between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end.
items.rationale: The precondition covers every application task, supervised or not, because CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released and STK-SUP-007 before the application runs. A failed check is a start-up code-integrity fault. The integrity method and the reference value for the code image are not given in the inputs (OP-SYS-005); this item states the obligation only.

items.text: Before releasing any application task after a reset, the controller shall check the configuration data block against its stored CRC-32 computed with the polynomial 0x04C11DB7.
items.rationale: The precondition covers every application task, supervised or not, because CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released and STK-SUP-007 before the application runs. A mismatch is a configuration-integrity fault. CRC-32 parameters other than the polynomial are not given (OP-SYS-005). The bytes the CRC covers, their serialization and the treatment of the stored CRC field are also open in OP-SYS-005 (F-sys-req-set-r1-005); until they are decided, valid and invalid blocks cannot be produced reproducibly and this item stays open. Validity and precedence when this check fails and a range violation is also observed: OP-SYS-040.

items.text: The start-up code integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 shall cover every byte of the application program code image between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end, for any image size up to 1 MiB.
items.rationale: Split from the former combined item: this item covers the start-up check only; coverage by each full pass of the run-time check is SYS-MEM-007. The 1 MiB limit is the CON-SUP-107 maximum image size.

items.text: Each full pass of the run-time code integrity check of SYS-MEM-005 shall cover every byte of the application program code image between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end, for any image size up to 1 MiB.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-MEM-003 so that run-time coverage is judged independently of start-up coverage. The 1 MiB limit is the CON-SUP-107 maximum image size; CON-SUP-108 defines the full pass. The pass completion time is SYS-MEM-005.

items.text: After a reset, the controller shall release no application task, supervised or not, until the start-up code integrity check of SYS-MEM-001 has completed over the whole application program code image without detecting a start-up code-integrity fault, the configuration integrity check of SYS-MEM-002 has completed without detecting a configuration-integrity fault, and the configuration range check of SYS-CFG-008 has completed over every task identifier, task period and timing limit in the configuration data block without detecting a configuration-range fault.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-006 and F-sys-req-item-r3-003 (the requirement text is unchanged; the valid-start verification now checks the order of check completion and first release). SYS-CFG-008 states only the conditions under which a configuration-range fault is detected, so 'SYS-CFG-008 has passed' did not say when the range check is finished: with a valid block, the absence of a fault at a given instant could mean either that the check found no fault or that it had not yet examined every value. The release condition now states a successful outcome for each start-up check that includes its completion: (1) the code integrity check has processed the whole image between __app_start and __app_end (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-003) and found no start-up code-integrity fault; (2) the configuration integrity check has compared the block with its stored CRC-32 (SYS-MEM-002) and found no configuration-integrity fault; (3) the range check has examined every task identifier, every task period and every timing limit in the configuration data block, which are the values that the CON-SUP-115 conditions apply to (SYS-CFG-008), and found no configuration-range fault. Release on a partly completed check therefore fails this item. In this set, 'the start-up checks have passed' means the instant at which all three outcomes hold; SYS-SUP-001, SYS-MEM-005, SYS-SAFE-004, SYS-SAFE-005 and SYS-SAFE-006 use it in this sense, and it is the instant at which CON-SUP-102 starts alive supervision. The release gate covers every application task, not only the tasks named as supervised in the configuration data block, because CON-SUP-107 requires the integrity checks before any task is released and STK-SUP-007 requires them before the application runs; since STK-SUP-004 makes supervision membership a configuration choice, a gate limited to supervised tasks would let an unsupervised application task start before the checks. This matches the preconditions of SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002 and SYS-CFG-008. The approved set of task identifiers used by the range check is open in OP-SYS-014, whether the CON-SUP-115 list of out-of-range conditions is exhaustive in OP-SYS-011, and the integrity method and reference values in OP-SYS-005; these change what each check examines, not the release condition stated here. Verification: through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), inject in separate runs a range fault in the first and in the last task entry of the configuration data block, for each of the three CON-SUP-115 conditions, a configuration CRC mismatch, and a code-image mismatch in the first and in the last byte before __app_end, and check that no application task is released after the reset. The order in which a check examines values is a design choice, so faults are placed at both ends; a release before a check has examined the faulty value fails the test. Valid-start test (default configuration, intact image and block, no fault injected, on the Renode simulator per CON-SUP-116): after the reset, record on one simulated time base (a) the completion event of the code integrity check over the whole image with no start-up code-integrity fault, (b) the completion event of the configuration integrity check with no configuration-integrity fault, (c) the completion event of the configuration range check over every task identifier, task period and timing limit with no configuration-range fault, and (d) the first release of any application task, supervised or not. Pass criteria: (d) is recorded, all of (a), (b) and (c) are recorded, and each of them precedes (d). The test fails if (d) occurs before any of (a), (b) or (c), or if any of them is missing when (d) occurs. A run in which no application task is released within the observation is inconclusive for the ordering check, neither passed nor failed (F-sys-req-set-r1-058): CON-SUP-107 and this item impose a release gate and give no deadline for the first release, so a missing release is not a failure of this item; the run is repeated with a longer observation or reported as not run. Progression to released and completed tasks after the start-up checks is judged by SYS-TEST-010 and SYS-TEST-011, not here. This catches a release made while one check is still running on a valid image, which the fault cases alone do not. The means by which a check's completion and a task's release are made observable in the test environment are not given by the inputs (SYS-TEST-002 provides fault-injection hooks only); this is recorded in OP-SYS-030 and does not change the release condition.

items.text: After the start-up checks have passed, the controller shall complete the first full pass of the run-time code integrity check of the application program code image within 11 s of the start of the first control cycle that starts at or after that instant, and each later full pass within 11 s of the completion of the full pass before it, for any image size up to 1 MiB.
items.rationale: Status open for OP-SYS-041 (F-sys-req-set-r1-003): whether this obligation applies when the start-up checks pass while the safe state is latched is not given by the inputs; also OP-SYS-005 (integrity method). Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-004 (requirement text unchanged; the verification now observes successful full-pass completions instead of fault detection). Earlier reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-007 (and F-sys-req-item-r1-009). The former text bounded only the duration of each pass, so the wait before the first pass and the gap between passes were unbounded. Split: this item keeps the pass completion bound and now anchors it to the start of run-time checking and to the end of the previous pass; the segment cadence that produces it is SYS-MEM-008, the controlled reference to CON-SUP-108. (1) First pass: under SYS-MEM-008 the first pass processes its first segment in the first control cycle that starts at or after the start-up checks have passed (SYS-MEM-004 defines that instant). An image of S bytes, at most 1 MiB (CON-SUP-107), needs ceil(S / 1 KiB) consecutive control cycles, at most 1024; at the 10 ms control cycle (CON-SUP-101) the first pass completes no later than 10.24 s after the start of its first control cycle. (2) Later passes: under SYS-MEM-008 every control cycle processes a segment and a new pass begins in the control cycle after the one that completed the previous pass, so there is no control cycle without run-time checking; the completion of a pass is at most 1024 control cycles plus less than one control cycle after the completion of the pass before it, at most 10.25 s. Both values are within the 11 s of CON-SUP-108, which this item applies from completion to completion so that the gap between passes is included, not only the duration of a pass. (3) The interval from the start-up checks passing to the start of the first control cycle is not given by the inputs and is already open in OP-SYS-020 (a); the bound therefore counts from the start of that control cycle and no new open point is raised. A failed run-time check is a run-time code-integrity fault (code 7, CON-SUP-112); the integrity method is open (OP-SYS-005). Verification (fault-free run on the Renode simulator per CON-SUP-116, default configuration, intact image and configuration data block, no fault injected), once with a 1 MiB image and once with a smaller image whose size is not a multiple of 1 KiB: record on one simulated time base (a) the instant the start-up checks have passed (SYS-MEM-004), (b) the start of every control cycle, and (c) for every control cycle, the start address and end address of every image range processed by the run-time check (the range record of SYS-MEM-008). A verified completion (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-059) is the instant at which processing of the range ending at __app_end ends, counted only when the range record shows that the ranges of that pass, in consecutive control cycles from the range beginning at __app_start, cover every byte from __app_start to __app_end without gap or repetition, and no run-time code-integrity fault is detected; processing the segment ending at __app_end alone is not a completion (CON-SUP-108, SYS-MEM-007). Run until at least three verified completions are recorded. Pass criteria: the first verified completion c1 is no later than 11 s after the start of the first control cycle that starts at or after (a); each later verified completion cn is no later than 11 s after the verified completion cn-1 before it; no run-time code-integrity fault (code 7) is reported. The test fails if no verified completion is recorded by the end of its 11 s window measured from that origin; a pass whose ranges do not cover the whole image is not a completion and does not end that window. Detection of an injected fault is not used for this item, because it shows neither the completion time of the preceding pass nor that a full pass completes; per-segment fault detection is verified under SYS-MEM-008. The means by which the start of a control cycle and the completion of a run-time pass are made observable are not given by the inputs (SYS-TEST-002 provides fault-injection hooks only; the fault report of SYS-DIAG-002 reports faults, not completions); this is recorded in OP-SYS-031, and the range record in OP-SYS-032; neither changes the bound.

items.text: In every control cycle that starts at or after the instant the start-up checks have passed, the controller shall process exactly one segment of the application program code image for the run-time code integrity check, taking the segment that begins at __app_start in the first such control cycle and in each control cycle that follows the processing of the segment ending at __app_end, and otherwise the segment that begins where the segment of the previous control cycle ended, where each segment is 1 KiB long except a last segment of a pass, which ends at __app_end and is at most 1 KiB long.
items.rationale: Status open for OP-SYS-041 (F-sys-req-set-r1-003): whether this obligation applies when the start-up checks pass while the safe state is latched is not given by the inputs; also OP-SYS-005 (integrity method). Split from SYS-MEM-005 for F-sys-req-item-r2-007. States the CON-SUP-108 cadence of one 1 KiB segment per control cycle as a system obligation, so the start of the first run-time pass and the continuation of later passes are defined: the first pass starts in the first control cycle that starts at or after the start-up checks have passed (the instant defined in SYS-MEM-004; run-time checking applies while running, STK-SUP-008), and each later pass starts at __app_start in the control cycle after the one that processed the last segment of the previous pass, so no control cycle after that instant is without a processed segment. The image need not be a multiple of 1 KiB (CON-SUP-107 bounds only its maximum size), so the last segment of a pass ends at __app_end and may be shorter; the segments of one pass together cover the whole image (SYS-MEM-007). The interval from the start-up checks passing to the start of the first control cycle is open in OP-SYS-020 (a). The processor time per control cycle is SYS-MEM-006 and the resulting pass completion bound is SYS-MEM-005. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-023 (requirement text unchanged; the verification now observes the processed range and the number of processed segments in every control cycle across pass boundaries, because a fault detected in the expected cycle for one segment does not show that no other segment was processed in a cycle, nor that the last segment and the restart of the next pass are correct). Verification (fault-free runs on the Renode simulator per CON-SUP-116, default configuration, intact image and configuration data block, no fault injected), run once with an image of S bytes where S is not a multiple of 1 KiB (so the last segment of a pass is shorter than 1 KiB) and once with a 1 MiB image: record on one simulated time base (a) the instant the start-up checks have passed (SYS-MEM-004), (b) the start of every control cycle, and (c) for every control cycle, the start address and end address of every image range processed by the run-time code integrity check in that cycle. Run until the first control cycle of the third pass has been recorded, so that at least two pass boundaries are crossed. Let N = ceil(S / 1 KiB). Pass criteria: (1) no image range is processed by the run-time check in a control cycle that starts before (a); (2) every recorded control cycle that starts at or after (a) contains exactly one processed range; (3) the range of the first control cycle that starts at or after (a) begins at __app_start; (4) in every later control cycle, the range begins at __app_start if the range of the previous control cycle ended at __app_end, and otherwise begins at the end address of the range of the previous control cycle; (5) every range is 1 KiB long except a range that ends at __app_end, which is S - (N - 1) x 1 KiB long; (6) no range lies outside __app_start to __app_end; (7) each pass consists of exactly N consecutive control cycles, its N-th range ends at __app_end, and the next pass begins at __app_start in the control cycle immediately after that one. The test fails if any control cycle at or after (a) contains zero or more than one processed range, if a range other than the one ending at __app_end is shorter than 1 KiB, if a range is skipped, repeated or out of order, if a pass ends anywhere other than __app_end, or if the next pass starts later than the following control cycle or anywhere other than __app_start. Supplementary fault case (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-060): the segment cadence is verified by the range record above, not by the fault report. With the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), inject in separate runs a run-time code-integrity fault into the first segment, into the last (partial) segment, and into a chosen intermediate segment; record the range record and the completion instant of the integrity computation that fails for the corrupted bytes, which depends on the integrity method open in OP-SYS-005 (for example a comparison per segment in the cycle that processed it, or a comparison at the end of the pass). Pass: the range record shows the corrupted segment processed in the control cycle that the cadence above assigns to it; a code 7 report (CON-SUP-112) is transmitted within 10 ms of the completion of that failing computation (SYS-DIAG-002, CON-SUP-105; start or end of transmission per OP-SYS-007); no code 7 report is transmitted before the corrupted segment has been processed. The failing computation is identified once OP-SYS-005 selects the method. The means by which the processed range of each control cycle is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator are not given by the inputs; this is recorded in OP-SYS-032 (control-cycle starts are already open in OP-SYS-031) and does not change the requirement.

items.text: The run-time code integrity check shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time per control cycle.
items.rationale: Makes 'without disturbing the application timing' of STK-SUP-008 measurable with the budget decided in CON-SUP-108.

items.text: After the start-up checks have passed, when a supervised task has completed no execution in each of 2 consecutive periods of its own, the controller shall detect an alive fault for that task at the end of the second of those periods, where a period of a task runs from the start of a control cycle in which the configured schedule defined in SYS-CFG-001 places a release of that task to the start of the next control cycle in which the configured schedule defined in SYS-CFG-001 places a release of that task, and the first period counted is the first period of that task that starts at or after the instant the start-up checks have passed.
items.rationale: Status open for OP-SYS-041 (F-sys-req-set-r1-003): whether alive supervision runs when the start-up checks pass while the safe state is latched is not given by the inputs; also OP-SYS-020. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-011: the alive-window boundaries are now defined. (1) Period boundaries: CON-SUP-101 makes the 10 ms period the control cycle and releases T_DIAG in every tenth control cycle, so a period of a task is bounded by the starts of the control cycles in which its release is scheduled: one control cycle for a 10 ms task, 10 control cycles for T_DIAG with the defaults (SYS-CFG-002, SYS-CFG-003). The boundaries follow the configured schedule (SYS-CFG-001), not the actual releases, so a task that is no longer released still reaches the end of its window. The position of a release inside its control cycle (OP-SYS-013 (d)) does not move the boundaries. (2) First window: CON-SUP-102 starts alive supervision when the start-up checks have passed, and no task is released before then (CON-SUP-107, SYS-MEM-004), so a period that starts before that instant contains no scheduled release at or after it; counting starts with the first period that starts at or after that instant. (3) Detection instant: the end of the second period is the end of the alive window, the instant from which CON-SUP-105 counts the 50 ms reaction (SYS-SAFE-001, SYS-SAFE-002). The inputs do not give the interval from the start-up checks passing to the start of the first control cycle, nor in which control cycle after start-up the first release of T_DIAG is scheduled; both set the latest instant of a first alive fault after start-up and are recorded in OP-SYS-020. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-001: the period boundaries now name the configured schedule defined in SYS-CFG-001, the same schedule that SYS-SUP-005 uses for the expected checkpoints, so alive and program-flow supervision use one release schedule. Whether a changed configured period also changes the application releases of the timer-driven scheduler (CON-SUP-006), and which periods are supported, is recorded in OP-SYS-046.

items.text: When the measured start delay of a release of a supervised task first exceeds the configured start limit of the task, whether the task has not yet begun executing for that release at that instant or begins executing at that instant, the controller shall detect exactly one late-start fault for that release without waiting for the task to begin executing, where, until the task begins executing for that release, its measured start delay is the time elapsed since that release measured as in SYS-SUP-004.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-010 and F-sys-req-item-r3-011 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r2-022, F-sys-req-item-r2-023, F-sys-req-item-r1-012). (1) Trigger: the start delay of a release is the time from the release of the task to the instant it begins executing; until the task begins it is the time elapsed since the release, measured as in SYS-SUP-004 (100 µs resolution, CON-SUP-103). The trigger instant T_x of a release is the first instant at which this measured value exceeds the start limit. The former text required that the task had not begun by that instant, so a task beginning exactly at T_x, whose measured start delay is above the limit and which CON-SUP-103 classifies as a late start, met neither that trigger nor SYS-SUP-006 (which covers only a measured start delay not greater than the limit). The trigger is now the measured start delay first exceeding the limit, in both cases: (a) the task has not begun at T_x (pending release, including a task that never begins and a task that begins later), and (b) the task begins at T_x. A task that begins before T_x has a measured start delay not greater than the limit and is SYS-SUP-006. Together the two items partition every release that begins or reaches T_x. (2) One declaration per release: 'exactly one' means that when a pending release has already been declared late, the later start of the task, whose measured start delay is then also above the limit, does not give a second late-start fault for that release; and a task that begins at T_x gives one declaration, not one from the elapsed-time comparison and another from the start-delay comparison. (3) Without waiting: for a pending release the declaration does not depend on the task beginning; for case (b) the task has begun at T_x, so the declaration is at or after the start. T_x lies at or after the expiry of the start limit (release plus configured limit); by how much depends on the mapping and alignment of the 100 µs measurement steps, open in OP-SYS-027. (4) Boundary: CON-SUP-103 allows a start 'at most' the limit after release and makes only a start 'later than the limit' a late start, so a measured start delay equal to the limit is in time; that case is SYS-SUP-006. (5) Measurement resolution and detection latency are separate. The 100 µs resolution of CON-SUP-103, stated in SYS-SUP-004, fixes the granularity of the measured start delay that is compared with the start limit; it gives no bound on when the controller evaluates that comparison or declares the fault. The former bound 'no later than 100 µs after the expiry of that start limit' was derived from the resolution alone and is removed. No input gives a deadline from the expiry of the start limit to the declaration of a late-start fault: CON-SUP-103 does not say when a late start is detected, and CON-SUP-105 makes the expiry of the timing limit the origin of the 50 ms safe-state reaction, not a detection deadline. The detection deadline is recorded as unresolved in OP-SYS-025, and this item stays open until it is decided. Whatever the detection latency, it lies inside the budgets that CON-SUP-105 counts from the expiry of the start limit: both control outputs low (SYS-SAFE-001) and the status signal low (SYS-SAFE-002) within 50 ms of that expiry. (6) Scope: a scheduled release that does not occur gives no start delay; such a task completes no execution and is covered by the alive fault of SYS-SUP-001. The release instant of T_CTRL and T_OUT relative to the start of the control cycle is open in OP-SYS-013 (d). Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build, default configuration and the late-start test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), for one supervised task and one release. Record on the simulator's virtual time base: the release instant; the expiry instant of the start limit (release instant plus configured start limit), recorded separately from T_x; the measured elapsed time since the release and, once the task begins, its measured start delay (readout as in SYS-SUP-004), from which T_x is taken; the instant the task begins executing, where it does; every instant at which the controller declares a late-start fault for that release, observed directly at the declaration and not taken from the fault report; every fault report with code 2 on the diagnostic serial line; the reset that follows the safe state; and the levels of both control outputs and the status signal. The fault report is not used for timing: its first bit can follow the declaration by up to the 10 ms of SYS-DIAG-002, and the <ms since start> field has millisecond resolution only (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005). Runs: (H) pending release, held: hold the task unstarted after its release until the reset that follows the safe state; record T_x, the declaration instant D_h and the reset instant X_h. (C) start coincident with T_x: start the task at the T_x recorded in run H (the simulator is deterministic for the same build, configuration and release instant); confirm from the readout that the measured elapsed time just before the start did not exceed the limit and that the measured start delay of the release exceeds it. (D) pending release, delayed start after declaration: start the task at the midpoint between D_h and X_h of run H, so that a controller that does not wait for the start has declared the fault before the start and the start occurs before the reset. (S) start sweep: start the task, in separate runs, at injected start delays from the configured start limit to 200 µs above it in 10 µs steps (the above-limit half of the SYS-SUP-006 sweep). Pass: (1) in runs H and D, and in every run of C and S whose measured start delay exceeds the limit, exactly one late-start declaration and exactly one fault report with code 2 occur for that release; (2) every declaration lies at or after T_x of its run; (3) in run H the declaration occurs while the task has not begun executing; (4) in run D the declaration precedes the start of the task, and no further declaration for that release occurs at or after the start; a declaration at or after the start in run D fails the test, because it shows that the controller waited for the task to begin; (5) in run C the declaration lies at or after the start, which coincides with T_x; (6) runs of S whose measured start delay is not greater than the limit are judged under SYS-SUP-006. In runs H and D, both control outputs and the status signal are checked low within 50 ms of the expiry of the start limit (SYS-SAFE-001, SYS-SAFE-002). When OP-SYS-025 sets a detection deadline, every declaration instant is also compared with the origin that decision approves plus that deadline (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-064). OP-SYS-025 asks for a deadline from the expiry of the start limit, and T_x can lie up to one 100 µs measurement step after that expiry depending on OP-SYS-027, so T_x is used as the origin only if that decision makes it the origin; using T_x otherwise could accept an overdue declaration. The direct observation of the declaration instant and its time base are open in OP-SYS-025 (c); the readout of the measured elapsed time and start delay, and the placement of the task start on the virtual time base, are capabilities of the verification environment that the inputs do not state and the system qualification specification must show.

items.text: When a supervised task begins executing for a release and the start delay measured for that release as an integer multiple of 100 µs (SYS-SUP-004) is not greater than the configured start limit of the task, compared as durations in the same time unit without further rounding of either value, the controller shall not detect a late-start fault for that release of the task.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-030 (earlier split from SYS-SUP-002 for F-sys-req-item-r1-012). (1) Time representation: the value compared is the measured start delay of SYS-SUP-004, which takes only integer multiples of 100 µs (CON-SUP-103); the true start delay is not compared directly. The configured start limit is the duration held in the configuration data block (SYS-CFG-001). (2) Comparison rule at the limit: the two durations are compared in the same time unit with no further rounding of either value; the release is in time if and only if the measured start delay is not greater than the configured start limit, and late (SYS-SUP-002) if and only if it is greater. CON-SUP-103 allows a start 'at most' the limit and calls only a start 'later than the limit' late, so equality is in time. With the 2 ms default of SYS-CFG-005 (20 steps of 100 µs), a measured 2.0 ms is in time and a measured 2.1 ms is late. If a configured limit is not a multiple of 100 µs, the rule still decides: for a limit of 2.05 ms, a measured 2.0 ms is in time and a measured 2.1 ms is late; the limit is not rounded to the measurement grid. (3) Times between measurement steps: which measured value a true start delay between two multiples of 100 µs receives (truncation, rounding to nearest or rounding up), and where the steps are aligned relative to the release, is not given by the inputs and is already open in OP-SYS-027; it decides the measured value, and therefore the outcome, for a true start just after the limit, not the comparison rule stated here. No new open point is raised for it. (4) Configured value representation: the inputs do not say in which unit the start limit is held in the configuration data block, nor whether only multiples of 100 µs are allowed; this is recorded in OP-SYS-028. The rule in (2) gives a defined result for either answer. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build, use the late-start test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002) to start a supervised task, in separate runs, at injected start delays from 200 µs below to 200 µs above its configured start limit (2 ms with the default of SYS-CFG-005) in 10 µs steps, and read the start delay the controller measured for each release, with the same readout as SYS-SUP-004. Pass: in every run whose measured start delay is not greater than the configured start limit, including every run whose measured value equals the limit, no fault report with code 2 is transmitted for that release; runs with a greater measured value are judged under SYS-SUP-002. Repeat with a test configuration whose start limit is not a multiple of 100 µs if OP-SYS-028 allows such values. The test-build readout of the measured start delay is a capability of the verification environment that the system qualification specification must show; the inputs do not state it.

items.text: When the configured execution limit of a supervised task expires for a release while the task has not completed that execution, the controller shall detect an overrun fault for that release at the expiry of that execution limit, without waiting for the task to complete, where the execution limit expires at the instant the execution time of that release, counted from the instant the task begins executing with the execution-time measure decided in OP-SYS-013 (d), reaches the configured execution limit.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-024 and F-sys-req-item-r2-025 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r1-013). (1) Detection instant: CON-SUP-103 defines an overrun as an execution longer than the limit, detected when the limit expires, and CON-SUP-105 counts the 50 ms reaction from the expiry of the timing limit. The former trigger (measured execution time exceeding the limit) and the former bound 'no later than 100 µs after the expiry' were derived from the 100 µs measurement resolution alone; no input authorizes that delay, so both are removed and the detection instant is the expiry itself. (2) Reconciliation with completion at the limit: at the expiry instant the execution time equals the limit. A task that has completed at or before that instant executed for at most the limit, is in time under CON-SUP-103 ('at most'), and gives no overrun (SYS-SUP-007). A task that has not completed at that instant can only complete with an execution time longer than the limit, so it is an overrun and can be decided at the expiry without waiting. A completion at the expiry instant itself counts as completed at the expiry and is in time. Detection at expiry and in-time completion at the limit therefore do not conflict, and no wait beyond the expiry is needed. A later completion does not repeat the detection for that release. (3) Execution-time measure: whether execution time counts the task's own processor time or the elapsed time from its start including preemption is open in OP-SYS-013 (d) (blocking). The expiry instant depends on that decision: with elapsed time it is the start of execution plus the limit; with processor time it is later by the time the task was preempted. The 100 µs resolution of SYS-SUP-004 is the granularity of the measured execution time; it is not a detection latency. (4) Detection latency: an implementation cannot declare the fault at exactly the expiry instant. No input approves a latency or tolerance between the expiry and the declaration of the overrun; that decision is recorded in OP-SYS-026, and this item stays open until OP-SYS-013 (d) and OP-SYS-026 are decided. Whatever the latency, it lies inside the budgets that CON-SUP-105 counts from the expiry: both control outputs low (SYS-SAFE-001) and the status signal low (SYS-SAFE-002) within 50 ms of the expiry. (5) Scope: a release that never begins executing is covered by the late-start fault of SYS-SUP-002 and, if no execution completes, by the alive fault of SYS-SUP-001. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with the overrun test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), in one run hold a supervised task executing for a release until the end of the observation, and in another run let it complete 1 ms of execution time after its execution limit. Record on the simulator's virtual time base the instant the task begins executing, every interval in which the task is preempted or resumed, its completion where it occurs, the instant the controller declares the overrun fault, the first bit of the fault report on the diagnostic serial line, and the levels of both control outputs and the status signal. Establish the expiry instant from these records with the execution-time measure decided in OP-SYS-013 (d), not as execution start plus the limit unless that decision is elapsed time. The declaration instant is observed directly, not taken from the fault report: the <ms since start> field has millisecond resolution only (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005), and the first bit of the report follows the declaration. Pass: in each run exactly one fault report with code 3 is transmitted for that release; the declaration instant lies at or after the expiry and within the tolerance decided in OP-SYS-026; in the run with late completion the declaration precedes the completion; and both control outputs and the status signal are low within 50 ms of the expiry (SYS-SAFE-001, SYS-SAFE-002). Time-stamping the task start, preemption, completion and fault declaration on the virtual time base with a resolution finer than the OP-SYS-026 tolerance is a capability of the verification environment; the inputs do not state it, and the system qualification specification must show it.

items.text: When the execution time of a release of a supervised task, measured under SYS-SUP-008 from the instant it begins executing to its completion at or before the expiry of its configured execution limit under SYS-SUP-003, is equal to or less than that execution limit, the controller shall not detect an overrun fault for that release, where a release that has not completed at that expiry has no such completion measurement, the value measured at that expiry is not a completion measurement, and the overrun detection of SYS-SUP-003 at that expiry applies to that release.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-003 (F-sys-req-item-r1-013) to state how a completion exactly at the allowed limit is treated. CON-SUP-103 allows execution 'at most' the limit and defines an overrun as an execution 'longer than the limit'; execution times are measured with a 100 µs resolution (CON-SUP-103, SYS-SUP-004). A measured execution time equal to the limit is therefore in time. The execution-time measure (processor time or elapsed time) is open in OP-SYS-013 (d). Verification: through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), let a supervised task complete at a measured execution time equal to its configured execution limit (3 ms for a 10 ms task with the default of SYS-CFG-006, 20 ms for T_DIAG with the default of SYS-CFG-007) and check that no fault report with code 3 is transmitted for that release. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-009. SYS-SUP-008 ends the measurement at the completion or at the expiry of the execution limit, whichever occurs first, so for a release that completes after the expiry the last measured value is taken at the expiry and equals the limit at the 100 µs resolution. The former text compared any measured execution time of a completed execution with the limit and could be read as exempting such a release, suppressing the overrun of CON-SUP-103. The comparison now applies only to a completion measurement: a measurement that ended at the completion of the release at or before the expiry; a completion at the expiry instant itself is in time (SYS-SUP-003 (2)). A release still executing at the expiry has no completion measurement, the value measured at the expiry does not count as one, and SYS-SUP-003 detects the overrun at the expiry. Added verification: in two further runs with the overrun test hook, let the release complete 100 µs and 1 ms of execution time after the expiry of its configured execution limit, and record the expiry, the overrun declaration and the completion as in SYS-SUP-003. Pass: in each run exactly one fault report with code 3 is transmitted for that release and the overrun declaration is recorded at or after the expiry and before the completion; a run in which the release completing after the expiry gives no code 3 fails this item.

items.text: The controller shall measure the start delay of each release of a supervised task with a resolution of 100 µs, so that each measured start delay is an integer multiple of 100 µs.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-014 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r2-026, F-sys-req-item-r2-027, F-sys-req-item-r1-014). (1) Split: the former item combined the resolution of the start delay and of the execution time; either could meet CON-SUP-103 while the other failed. This item keeps the start delay; the execution time is SYS-SUP-008. (2) Meaning of the resolution: CON-SUP-103 gives a 100 µs resolution with no 'or finer', so a measured start delay takes only integer multiples of 100 µs and the measurement increment is 100 µs; a finer step (values between multiples) and a coarser step (no two measurable values 100 µs apart) both fail this item. The start delay of a release is the time from the release of the task to the instant it begins executing (SYS-SUP-002). (3) Mapping and alignment: how a true start delay that lies between two multiples of 100 µs is mapped to a measured value (truncation, rounding to nearest or rounding up), and where the 100 µs steps are aligned relative to the release, is not given by the inputs and is already recorded in OP-SYS-027; no new open point is raised. It does not change the resolution required here, but it decides whether a start up to 100 µs after the start limit is judged late (SYS-SUP-002, SYS-SUP-006). (4) Scope of the verification (F-sys-req-item-r3-014): this item requires the 100 µs measurement increment only. The former pass criteria that the measured value does not decrease as the injected start delay increases, that the sweep yields 4 or 5 distinct measured values with adjacent values exactly 100 µs apart, and that every measured value differs from its injected start delay by less than 100 µs are properties of the input-to-output mapping, the alignment and the measurement error, which CON-SUP-103 does not state and OP-SYS-027 leaves undecided; they could reject a measurement that meets the stated resolution, so they are removed from this item. No mapping, alignment or error tolerance is proposed here; error and mapping criteria are applied once OP-SYS-027 is decided and gives them an approved basis. Testing only fault decisions at the limit and one 100 µs step above it (the version before F-sys-req-item-r1-014) is not used, because a finer measurement also passes it; the increment is verified from the measured values themselves. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build, use the late-start test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002) to start a supervised task, in separate runs, at injected start delays from 200 µs below to 200 µs above its configured start limit in 10 µs steps (41 runs), read the start delay the controller measured for each release, and record on the virtual time base, independently of that readout, the release instant and the instant the task begins executing, whose difference is the release-to-start interval of the run. Pass: (a) every measured start delay is an integer multiple of 100 µs, so no finer step occurs; (b) at least two of the measured start delays differ by exactly 100 µs, so the 100 µs increment occurs and the step is not coarser; (c) in every run the measured start delay differs from the recorded release-to-start interval by less than 100 µs; (d) once OP-SYS-027 is decided, every measured value equals the value that the approved mapping and alignment assign to the recorded interval. A finer measurement fails (a); a step coarser than 100 µs fails (b); a readout that does not follow the release-to-start interval, or is measured from another event, fails (c), for example an output alternating between 0 and 100 µs whatever the injected delay. The recorded interval must be resolved on the virtual time base finer than 10 µs; the 400 µs sweep makes the true start delays span several 100 µs steps. The fault report does not carry the measured value (CON-SUP-112 gives milliseconds since start only), and no input provides a test-build readout of the measured start delay; it is a capability of the verification environment that the system qualification specification must show. (5) Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-065: criteria (a) and (b) alone accept a readout that does not depend on the measured interval. Tracking criterion (c) is added in a form that holds for every mapping (truncation, rounding to nearest, rounding up) and every alignment of the 100 µs steps relative to the release, because each of them places the measured value less than one step from the interval it measures; it therefore does not presuppose the decision in OP-SYS-027, and its confirmation is part of that open point. The monotonicity and distinct-count criteria removed in (4) are not restored; the approved mapping is applied by criterion (d) when it is decided.

items.text: For each release of a supervised task that begins executing, the controller shall measure the execution time of that release from the instant it begins executing until it completes or its configured execution limit expires, whichever occurs first, with a resolution of 100 µs, so that each measured execution time is an integer multiple of 100 µs.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-027 and F-sys-req-item-r3-028. (R3-a) Scope and end of the measurement (F-sys-req-item-r3-027): the text now states which releases are measured and when the measurement ends. (i) Releases measured: only a release that begins executing has an execution time. A release that never begins executing has no execution time to measure and is outside this item; it is handled by the late-start check (SYS-SUP-002, SYS-SUP-006) and alive supervision (SYS-SUP-001). (ii) End of the measurement: the measurement ends when the release completes or when its configured execution limit expires, whichever occurs first. CON-SUP-103 defines an overrun as an execution longer than the limit, detected when the limit expires (SYS-SUP-003). The measurement up to the expiry is what that decision needs. (iii) Value at overrun completion: no input uses an execution-time value after the expiry of the limit. The fault report does not carry it (CON-SUP-112), and the overrun is decided at the expiry. So this item does not require a value at the completion of an overrunning release. It neither requires nor forbids continued measurement after the expiry. The verification reads the value at the expiry for overrunning releases. Requiring a value at completion would add an obligation that the inputs do not state, so none is proposed. (R3-b) Scope of the verification (F-sys-req-item-r3-028): this item now requires only the 100 µs measurement increment, as in SYS-SUP-004 after F-sys-req-item-r3-014. The former pass criteria checked that measured values did not decrease as the injected execution time increased, that the sweep yielded 4 or 5 distinct values, and that each measured value differed from its injected execution time by less than 100 µs. These are properties of the input-to-output mapping, the alignment and the measurement error. CON-SUP-103 does not state them and OP-SYS-027 leaves them undecided. They could reject a measurement that meets the stated resolution, so they are removed. No mapping, alignment or error tolerance is proposed here. Accuracy and mapping criteria will apply once OP-SYS-027 is decided and gives them an approved basis. No new open point is raised. Earlier history: split from SYS-SUP-004 for F-sys-req-item-r2-026 and F-sys-req-item-r2-027, so that the resolution of the execution-time measurement is traced and judged independently of the start-delay measurement. (1) Meaning of the resolution: as in SYS-SUP-004, CON-SUP-103 gives a 100 µs resolution with no 'or finer', so a measured execution time takes only integer multiples of 100 µs and the measurement increment is 100 µs; a finer step (values between multiples) and a coarser step (no two measurable values 100 µs apart) both fail this item. (2) Whether execution time counts the task's own processor time or the elapsed time from its start including preemption is open in OP-SYS-013 (d); the resolution and the end points required here apply to whichever measure is decided. How a true execution time between two multiples of 100 µs is mapped to a measured value, and where the 100 µs steps are aligned relative to the start of execution, is recorded in OP-SYS-027; it decides the overrun judgement near the limit (SYS-SUP-003, SYS-SUP-007), not the resolution. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build, use the overrun test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002) to let a supervised task begin executing and, in separate runs and without preemption so that processor time and elapsed time coincide, run for injected execution times. Sweep runs: completion at injected execution times from 400 µs below its configured execution limit up to the limit in 10 µs steps (41 runs); every sweep run completes no later than the expiry, so its measurement ends at completion. For each sweep run, read the execution time the controller measured for that release. Overrun runs: injected execution times of 100 µs, 200 µs and 1 ms above the configured execution limit (3 runs); for each, read the execution time the controller has measured for that release at the expiry of its execution limit. No value at the completion of an overrunning release is read or required. In every run, record on the virtual time base, independently of the controller's readout, the instant the task begins executing and either its completion (sweep runs) or the expiry of its configured execution limit (overrun runs), established as in SYS-SUP-003; without preemption, processor time and elapsed time give the same instants. Pass: (a) every measured execution time of the sweep runs and the overrun runs is an integer multiple of 100 µs, so no finer step occurs; (b) at least two measured execution times of the sweep runs differ by exactly 100 µs, so the 100 µs increment occurs and the step is not coarser; (c) the measured execution time of each sweep run differs from its recorded start-to-completion interval, and the value read at the expiry in each overrun run differs from its recorded start-to-expiry interval, by less than 100 µs; (d) once OP-SYS-027 is decided, every measured value equals the value that the approved mapping and alignment assign to the recorded interval. A finer measurement fails (a); a step coarser than 100 µs fails (b); a readout unrelated to the execution time, or measured from another start event, fails (c). The recorded intervals must be resolved on the virtual time base finer than 10 µs; the 400 µs sweep makes the true execution times span 4 steps of 100 µs. The fault report does not carry the measured value (CON-SUP-112), and no input provides a test-build readout of the measured execution time, including its value at the expiry of the limit. That readout is a capability of the verification environment that the system qualification specification must show. (R4) Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-067: criteria (a) and (b) alone accept values unrelated to the execution time or measured from the wrong start event. Tracking criterion (c) compares the readout with independently recorded start-to-completion and start-to-expiry intervals; it holds for every mapping and alignment of the 100 µs steps, because each places the measured value less than one step from the interval it measures, so it does not presuppose OP-SYS-027, and its confirmation is part of that open point. The approved mapping is applied by criterion (d) when it is decided.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, the controller shall detect a program-flow fault when a checkpoint assigned to that control cycle has not arrived for that control cycle or the checkpoints that have arrived for that control cycle are in an order other than the configured checkpoint order, where the checkpoints assigned to a control cycle are those of every release that the configured schedule (SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-009) schedules in that control cycle, whether or not that release occurs, so that a scheduled release that does not occur leaves its checkpoint not arrived for that control cycle, a checkpoint received by the supervisor strictly before the end of its assigned control cycle has arrived for that control cycle, a checkpoint received strictly after that end has not arrived for that control cycle, and a checkpoint received at the instant of that end is classified by the precedence rule between receipt and evaluation decided in OP-SYS-036.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-001 (STK-SUP-003, skipped task). The expected checkpoint set of a control cycle is now defined from the configured schedule, not from the observed releases: CON-SUP-104 checks 'the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle', and CON-SUP-101 and the configuration (SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-004, SYS-CFG-009) state which releases occur in each cycle, so a release scheduled in a cycle is expected whether or not it occurs. A checkpoint received for a release that did occur belongs to the cycle in which that release was scheduled (point (2) below is updated accordingly). End-of-cycle verdict for a scheduled release that never occurs: its checkpoint has not arrived for that cycle, so the controller detects a program-flow fault (code 4) at the end of that cycle, the same verdict as for a release whose checkpoint fails to arrive. The late-start rule of SYS-SUP-002 does not apply to it, because no release occurred to measure a start delay from; the alive rule (SYS-SUP-001) can apply only after a second period. Added verification run (F3), separate from F1: with the program-flow hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002) suppress the release of one task scheduled in control cycle N (T_CTRL in a cycle without T_DIAG), so that the task is not released in cycle N; record the scheduled releases from the configuration, the actual releases, the receipt of every checkpoint and every program-flow declaration. Pass F3: the record shows no release of that task in cycle N and exactly one program-flow fault declaration for cycle N at its end instant; a run in which the task is released in cycle N is invalid for F3, not passed. F1 (release occurs, checkpoint withheld) stays a separate run, so the two causes are verified separately. Whether the hook can suppress a release rather than a checkpoint is part of the injected behaviour that CON-SUP-116 leaves to the test build; the system qualification specification must show it. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-015 and F-sys-req-item-r3-016 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r2-028, F-sys-req-item-r1-015). (R3-a) Coincident receipt and evaluation (F-sys-req-item-r3-015): the former text counted a checkpoint received exactly at the end of its cycle as not arrived. CON-SUP-104 places the check at the end of the control cycle and CON-SUP-105 makes that end the detection instant, but neither input says whether a receipt at that same instant precedes or follows the evaluation, and the choice decides whether a code 4 fault is declared. That choice was the author's, not an approved rule, and is withdrawn. The text now fixes only the cases the inputs decide (received strictly before the end: arrived; strictly after: not arrived) and takes the coincident case from the precedence rule to be decided in OP-SYS-036 (blocking); this item stays open until it is decided. No precedence is proposed here. (R3-b) Exclusion of a late checkpoint from later cycles (F-sys-req-item-r3-016): split out to SYS-SUP-009, verified by analysis, because in the normal reaction sequence the flow evaluation of the following cycle need not occur (SYS-WDG-003 withholds the refresh at the end of the faulty cycle, SYS-WDG-006 and SYS-RST-001 can reset the controller before the end of the next cycle), so the absence of a second code 4 report does not show that the late checkpoint was discarded. This item keeps the per-cycle detection only; the former pass criterion 'no code 4 for the following cycle' is removed from its verification. The remaining points below are carried over from the earlier rework. (1) Arrival: a checkpoint is an indication that a supervised task signals to the supervisor; its arrival is the instant the supervisor receives that indication, not the instant the task issues it. The text and this rationale now use the same event. Receipt is chosen because CON-SUP-104 says the checkpoints 'must arrive', and arrival at the supervisor is the event the end-of-cycle check can observe. Any delay between the task issuing the signal and the supervisor receiving it counts against the task: a checkpoint issued before the end of its cycle but received strictly after that end is treated as missing in that cycle. (1a) Boundary: a checkpoint received strictly after the end of its assigned cycle has not arrived for that cycle, so that cycle has a flow fault (missing checkpoint); receipt at the end instant itself is OP-SYS-036. That a checkpoint which has not arrived for its assigned cycle is not counted in the check of any later cycle is SYS-SUP-009. Order is the order in which the supervisor received the checkpoints that have arrived for the cycle. When a task signals its checkpoint during its execution remains open, so whether a release that meets its timing limits can still deliver its checkpoint before the end of its cycle is unresolved (OP-SYS-021 (a) and (b)). This item fixes the decision for a given receipt instant; OP-SYS-021 can change which cycle a checkpoint is checked in. (2) Assignment to a control cycle: CON-SUP-104 checks 'the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle', so a checkpoint is assigned to the control cycle in which the configured schedule places the release of the task that supplies it, not to the cycle in which it arrives. A checkpoint is missing when it has not arrived by the end of the control cycle to which it is assigned, which is the instant CON-SUP-104 fixes for the check and CON-SUP-105 uses as the detection instant. The expected checkpoints and their order per cycle come from the configured checkpoint order (SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-004). (3) Not given by the inputs: the point in a task's execution at which it signals its checkpoint (for example when it begins executing, at a point within its execution, or when it completes). This matters for T_DIAG: it is released after T_OUT (CON-SUP-101) and may start up to 2 ms after release and execute up to 20 ms (CON-SUP-103), longer than the 10 ms control cycle, so a checkpoint signalled late in its execution can arrive after the end of its release cycle and be detected as missing although the release meets its timing limits. The release instants inside the cycle are open in OP-SYS-013 (d). The event and the handling of a checkpoint that can arrive after its release cycle are recorded in OP-SYS-021; until it is resolved this item is open. Which task a flow fault names in its report is recorded in OP-SYS-008. Verification: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build and the program-flow test hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), default configuration. Record on the simulator's virtual time base the end instant of every control cycle, the receipt instant of every checkpoint with the control cycle of its task's release, every program-flow fault declaration observed directly at the declaration, and every fault report with code 4. The declaration is observed directly because the code 4 report can be cut off by the reset that follows (OP-SYS-004); where the report is transmitted it is checked against SYS-DIAG-002 and SYS-DIAG-005. Runs: (F1) withhold the checkpoint of one released task in one control cycle; (F3) suppress one scheduled release, as described at the start of this rationale; (F2) swap the receipt order of two checkpoints of one control cycle; (F0) a fault-free control cycle in which all assigned checkpoints are received in the configured order. Boundary runs, each with the last checkpoint of the configured order of one control cycle N (T_OUT in a cycle without T_DIAG): (B1) receipt 100 µs before the end of cycle N; (B2) receipt at the same virtual instant as the end of cycle N; (B3) receipt 100 µs after the end of cycle N; (B4) the task issues the checkpoint before the end of cycle N and its receipt is delayed to 100 µs after that end. Pass: F1, F2 and F3 each give exactly one program-flow fault declaration for that cycle at its end instant; F0 and B1 give no program-flow fault declaration for cycle N; B3 and B4 each give exactly one program-flow fault declaration for cycle N at its end instant; B2 gives the outcome that the rule decided in OP-SYS-036 assigns to a coincident receipt (no declaration for cycle N if receipt precedes evaluation, exactly one declaration for cycle N at its end instant if evaluation precedes receipt), and the run fails on any other outcome. B2 also confirms from the record that receipt and the end of cycle N carry the same virtual-time value at the comparison resolution decided in OP-SYS-036 (b); a run in which they differ is invalid, not passed. Whether cycle N+1 is evaluated after B3 or B4 is not judged here (SYS-SUP-009). The placement of a receipt at a given virtual instant, including the instant of the end of a cycle, the direct observation of the declaration and the readout of the receipt instant are capabilities of the verification environment that the inputs do not state; the system qualification specification must show them (see OP-SYS-036 (b), and OP-SYS-034 (a) and (b) for observation of the rule-defined fault event).

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, the controller shall check program flow using only the checkpoints that have arrived for that control cycle as defined in SYS-SUP-005, so that a checkpoint assigned to an earlier control cycle, including one received during that control cycle, is not counted as arrived, missing, extra or out of order in that check.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-005 for F-sys-req-item-r3-016. (1) Basis: CON-SUP-104 checks at the end of each control cycle 'the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle', so a checkpoint belongs to the cycle in which its release is scheduled (SYS-SUP-005) and plays no part in the check of any other cycle. A checkpoint that has not arrived for its assigned cycle N (received strictly after the end of cycle N, or at that end if OP-SYS-036 so decides) gives the missing-checkpoint fault of cycle N under SYS-SUP-005 and is excluded from the check of cycle N+1 and every later cycle, so a late checkpoint cannot also cause an extra-checkpoint or out-of-order decision in a later cycle. (2) Why analysis, not test: after a flow fault in cycle N, SYS-WDG-003 withholds the window-watchdog refresh at the end of cycle N, SYS-WDG-006 resets the controller once more than 12 ms have elapsed since the previous refresh, no later than the latest reset instant of OP-SYS-045, and SYS-RST-001 requests a software reset within 20 ms of safe-state entry; either reset can occur before the end of cycle N+1, which is the first check that the late checkpoint could reach. In the normal reaction sequence the check of cycle N+1 is therefore not guaranteed to take place, and the absence of a second code 4 report does not show that the late checkpoint was excluded. No input provides a test build that keeps the flow check running after a flow fault (CON-SUP-116 gives fault-injection hooks only), and none is proposed here. (3) Dependency: OP-SYS-021 (b) may decide that a checkpoint arriving after its release cycle is checked at the end of the cycle in which it arrives or of another configured cycle; that decision would change this item, which therefore stays open until OP-SYS-021 is decided. The coincident-receipt case is OP-SYS-036. Verification (analysis): on the software architecture and detailed design of the program-flow check (later stages), identify every path by which a received checkpoint can reach the end-of-cycle evaluation, including any buffer, counter, sequence index or order state that persists from one control cycle to the next. Pass: for every such path the analysis shows that (a) each received checkpoint is associated with the control cycle in which its release is scheduled (SYS-SUP-005); (b) the evaluation at the end of cycle M takes, for presence, absence, count and order, only checkpoints associated with cycle M that have arrived for cycle M; (c) for every state retained along that path from an earlier cycle N into cycle M (buffer, counter, sequence index, order state or cycle tag), the presence, count and order results of the evaluation of cycle M are the same as they would be if no checkpoint associated with any earlier cycle had been received; retained cycle-tagged state that is ignored before it can influence the evaluation meets this criterion. A path for which (a), (b) or (c) is not shown fails the analysis. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-068: the former criterion (d), which forbade carrying any order or count state of cycle N into the evaluation of cycle M, is withdrawn, because CON-SUP-104 limits what can affect the result of the check, not which state is retained. Supporting evidence for the analysis: host unit tests of the flow-check unit (CON-SUP-005), in which a checkpoint of cycle N is received after the end of cycle N and the evaluation of cycle N+1 is then executed with the checkpoints of cycle N+1 received in the configured order, and which show no missing, extra or out-of-order decision for cycle N+1; such tests are possible on the host because they do not depend on the watchdog or reset sequence. This evidence supports the analysis and does not replace it.

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault, the controller shall drive both control outputs low within 50 ms of the detection instant defined in CON-SUP-105.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-016 and split. This item now lists only the faults detected after the start-up checks have passed, each of which has a detectability instant in CON-SUP-105: end of the alive window (alive), expiry of the timing limit (late start, overrun), end of the control cycle (program flow), completion of the failing integrity computation (run-time code integrity). The start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity and configuration-range faults are detected before any task is released (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-CFG-008, CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-115), while CON-SUP-109 already holds both control outputs low (SYS-SAFE-004); their control-output obligation is SYS-SAFE-007, which needs no start event and so does not depend on the configuration-range detectability instant that CON-SUP-105 does not give (OP-SYS-017). 'Safe state' in this set: both control outputs low and the status signal low (STK-SUP-009, CON-SUP-109). For faults of this item the controller has entered the safe state when SYS-SAFE-001 and SYS-SAFE-002 are both met. A watchdog-reset fault is reported (SYS-RST-011) but is not listed here, because the inputs give no safe-state reaction for it.

items.text: When a start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity or configuration-range fault is detected, the controller shall keep both control outputs low without interruption from the reset that preceded the detection until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-001 (F-sys-req-item-r1-016). These three faults are detected before any task is released after a reset (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-CFG-008; CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-115). From any reset until the start-up checks pass, CON-SUP-109 holds both control outputs low (SYS-SAFE-004), and the checks do not pass when one of these faults is detected. The control outputs are therefore already off at the detection instant, so no output transition and no start event are needed: keeping them low from the preceding reset meets the 50 ms reaction of STK-SUP-009 for any detection instant, including the configuration-range fault for which CON-SUP-105 gives no detectability instant (OP-SYS-017). After the next reset, SYS-SAFE-004 applies again; a configuration-range fault latches the safe state (SYS-RST-003) and SYS-SAFE-003 holds the outputs low while it is latched. Verification: inject each of the three faults through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), record both control outputs from the reset onward, and check that neither output is high at any sample until the next reset.

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault, the controller shall drive the status signal low within 50 ms of the detection instant defined in CON-SUP-105.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-017 and split, in the same way as SYS-SAFE-001 and SYS-SAFE-007. This item now lists only the faults detected after the start-up checks have passed, each of which has a detectability instant in CON-SUP-105: end of the alive window (alive), expiry of the timing limit (late start, overrun), end of the control cycle (program flow), completion of the failing integrity computation (run-time code integrity). The start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity and configuration-range faults are detected before any task is released (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-CFG-008; CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-115), while CON-SUP-109 already holds the status signal low (SYS-SAFE-005); their status-signal obligation is SYS-SAFE-008, which needs no start event. The status-signal reaction therefore no longer depends on the configuration-range detectability instant that CON-SUP-105 does not give; OP-SYS-017 remains for the items that still measure from it (SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-DIAG-005). For faults of this item the controller has entered the safe state when SYS-SAFE-001 and SYS-SAFE-002 are both met.

items.text: When a start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity or configuration-range fault is detected, the controller shall keep the status signal low without interruption from the reset that preceded the detection until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-017); the status-signal counterpart of SYS-SAFE-007. These three faults are detected before any task is released after a reset (SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-CFG-008; CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-115). From any reset until the start-up checks pass, CON-SUP-109 holds the status signal low (SYS-SAFE-005), and the checks do not pass when one of these faults is detected, so SYS-SAFE-006 never drives the signal high. The status signal is therefore already low at the detection instant, so no transition and no start event are needed: keeping it low from the preceding reset meets the 50 ms reaction of STK-SUP-009 for any detection instant, including the configuration-range fault for which CON-SUP-105 gives no detectability instant (OP-SYS-017). After the next reset, SYS-SAFE-005 applies again; a configuration-range fault latches the safe state (SYS-RST-003) and SYS-SAFE-003 holds the status signal low while it is latched. Verification: inject each of the three faults through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), record the status signal from the reset onward, and check that it is not high at any sample until the next reset.

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault, the controller shall drive neither control output from low to high at any instant from the detection instant defined in CON-SUP-105, including that instant, until the next reset, excluding the instant of that reset.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-062: the interval now has explicit endpoints. It includes the detection instant, so a low-to-high transition coincident with the event is prohibited, as the verification already judged it. It ends at the next reset, exclusive, because from that reset SYS-SAFE-004 (and SYS-SAFE-010 while latched) holds both outputs low, so a transition at the reset instant is judged under those items and no instant is left without a hold obligation. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-015 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r1-018) and split. The former text held the outputs 'while the controller is in the safe state', and the safe state is defined in this set by the output and status levels (SYS-SAFE-001 rationale), so an output going high would itself end the hold interval. The hold interval is now bounded by events that do not depend on the output levels. (1) Entry: the detection instant of CON-SUP-105 for the faults of SYS-SAFE-001 (end of the alive window, expiry of the timing limit, end of the control cycle, completion of the failing integrity computation).
