From that instant no low-to-high transition is permitted on either control output; SYS-SAFE-001 requires both outputs low within 50 ms of the same instant, so the two items together keep each output low from the instant it is driven low until the exit event, and an output that is already low at detection stays low. (2) Exit, not latched: the next reset of any kind; STK-SUP-010 allows recovery only by a reset, the supervisor requests it under SYS-RST-001, and a watchdog reset (SYS-WDG-001, SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006) also ends the interval. From that reset SYS-SAFE-004 holds both outputs low until the start-up checks have passed, so no interval without a hold obligation exists. (3) Exit, latched: split to SYS-SAFE-010, which holds the outputs from the reset preceding the latching until the next power-on reset, across software and watchdog resets; references in SYS-SAFE-007, SYS-SAFE-008 and SYS-RST-012 to the hold of SYS-SAFE-003 while the safe state is latched are met by SYS-SAFE-010. (4) Start-up code-integrity and configuration-integrity faults are held by SYS-SAFE-007 from the preceding reset to the next reset. A watchdog-reset fault has no safe-state reaction (SYS-RST-011). The status signal hold is SYS-SAFE-009. Verification (reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-008): on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005, CON-SUP-116) record, on one common time base, the rule-defined fault event of CON-SUP-105 for the injected fault (end of the alive window, expiry of the timing limit, end of the control cycle, or completion of the failing integrity computation), every level change of each of the two simulated control outputs, and the next reset. The detection instant is taken from this event record, not from the millisecond <ms since start> field of the fault report (SYS-DIAG-005), whose resolution cannot order an output transition that lies close to the event. For each of the five faults (alive, late start, overrun, program flow, run-time code integrity), injected through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), run four cases that differ in the output levels at the event: both outputs high; first output low and second high; first output high and second low; both outputs low. In each case with an output low at the event, the test build requests that output high after the event, including a request at the first opportunity after it, so that a low output that stays low shows the hold and not the absence of a request. Pass criterion: in every case, no low-to-high transition of either control output is recorded at or after the event instant and before the next reset; a transition with the same time stamp as the event counts as after it; a transition with the same time stamp as the next reset is judged under SYS-SAFE-004 or SYS-SAFE-010. Transitions before the event are not judged by this item. Not given by the inputs and recorded in OP-SYS-034: how the rule-defined fault event is made observable in a test build or on the simulator, the common time base and its resolution, and how a test sets each control output high or low before the event and requests it high after the event, since no input states which part drives the control outputs in normal operation.

items.text: When the safe state is latched under SYS-RST-003 or SYS-RST-004, the controller shall keep both control outputs low without interruption from the reset that preceded the latching until the next power-on reset, across every software reset and watchdog reset in between.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-003 for F-sys-req-item-r2-015, to state the hold interval and the exit condition of the latched safe state by events independent of the output levels. (1) Entry: the reset that preceded the latching. For a configuration-range fault that is the reset before the start-up range check that detected it (SYS-CFG-008, SYS-RST-003); for repeated faults it is the third consecutive supervisor reset with the same fault code (SYS-RST-004, CON-SUP-110). Both control outputs are already held low from that reset (SYS-SAFE-004, SYS-SAFE-007), so no output transition is needed at latching. (2) Exit: the next power-on reset. CON-SUP-110 latches the safe state until a power-on reset and keeps the latch across software and watchdog resets (SYS-RST-005); STK-SUP-010 requires staying in the safe state until power-cycled; after a power-on reset the latch is cleared (SYS-RST-007) and SYS-SAFE-004 applies. A software or watchdog reset while latched, including the recurring watchdog resets of OP-SYS-010, does not end the interval. (3) Not given by the inputs: whether a reset classified as 'other' (CON-SUP-111) keeps the latch or counts as a power-on reset, recorded in OP-SYS-024, and which reset flags identify a power-on reset, OP-SYS-016. The feasibility of holding the outputs low while a reset is asserted and before software can act is OP-SYS-018; the hardware allocation covers that interval. The status-signal counterpart is SYS-SAFE-009. Verification: latch the safe state by a configuration-range fault and, separately, by three same-code supervisor resets (test hooks, CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002); then apply a software reset and an independent-watchdog and a window-watchdog reset; record both control outputs from the reset preceding the latching until a power-on reset and check that neither is high at any sample; after the power-on reset check that the latch is cleared. Status open: OP-SYS-024 (exit by an 'other' reset) and OP-SYS-041 (functions active when the start-up checks pass while latched).

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault, the controller shall not drive the status signal from low to high at any instant from the detection instant defined in CON-SUP-105, including that instant, until the next reset, excluding the instant of that reset.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-063: the interval now has explicit endpoints. It includes the detection instant, so a low-to-high transition coincident with the event is prohibited, as the verification already judged it. It ends at the next reset, exclusive, because from that reset SYS-SAFE-005 (and SYS-SAFE-011 while latched) holds the status signal low, so a transition at the reset instant is judged under those items and no instant is left without a hold obligation. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-020 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r1-018) and split, in the same way as SYS-SAFE-003 and SYS-SAFE-010. The former text held the status signal 'while the controller is in the safe state', and the safe state is defined in this set by the control-output and status-signal levels (SYS-SAFE-001 rationale), so the status signal going high would itself end the hold interval and leave the obligation undefined from then on. The hold interval is now bounded by events that do not depend on the signal levels. (1) Entry: the detection instant of CON-SUP-105 for the faults of SYS-SAFE-002 (end of the alive window, expiry of the timing limit, end of the control cycle, completion of the failing integrity computation). From that instant no low-to-high transition of the status signal is permitted; SYS-SAFE-002 requires the signal low within 50 ms of the same instant, so the two items together keep it low from the instant it is driven low until the exit event, and a signal already low at detection stays low. (2) Exit, not latched: the next reset of any kind; STK-SUP-010 allows recovery only by a reset, the supervisor requests it under SYS-RST-001, and a watchdog reset (SYS-WDG-001, SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006) also ends the interval. From that reset SYS-SAFE-005 holds the status signal low until the start-up checks have passed, and SYS-SAFE-006 drives it high only when the safe state is not latched, so no interval without a hold obligation exists. The pin level while a reset is asserted is OP-SYS-019. (3) Exit, latched: split to SYS-SAFE-011, which holds the status signal low from the reset preceding the latching until the next power-on reset, across software and watchdog resets (CON-SUP-110). The reference in SYS-SAFE-010 to its status-signal counterpart SYS-SAFE-009 is met for the latched case by SYS-SAFE-011, as is the reference in SYS-SAFE-008 to the status-signal hold while the safe state is latched. (4) Start-up code-integrity and configuration-integrity faults are held by SYS-SAFE-008 from the preceding reset to the next reset; a configuration-range fault is held by SYS-SAFE-008 and, once latched, by SYS-SAFE-011. A watchdog-reset fault has no safe-state reaction (SYS-RST-011). This item applies independently of the control-output levels, which are SYS-SAFE-001 and SYS-SAFE-003. Verification (reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-009): on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005, CON-SUP-116) record, on one common time base, the rule-defined fault event of CON-SUP-105 for the injected fault (end of the alive window, expiry of the timing limit, end of the control cycle, or completion of the failing integrity computation), every level change of the simulated status signal, and the next reset. The detection instant is taken from this event record, not from the millisecond <ms since start> field of the fault report (SYS-DIAG-005), whose resolution cannot order a status-signal transition that lies close to the event. For each of the five faults (alive, late start, overrun, program flow, run-time code integrity), injected through the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002), run two cases that differ in the status-signal level at the event: status signal high; status signal already low. In the already-low case the test build requests the status signal high after the event, including a request at the first opportunity after it, so that a signal that stays low shows the hold and not the absence of a request. Pass criterion: in every case, no low-to-high transition of the status signal is recorded at or after the event instant and before the next reset; a transition with the same time stamp as the event counts as after it; a transition with the same time stamp as the next reset is judged under SYS-SAFE-005 or SYS-SAFE-011. Transitions before the event are not judged by this item. Not given by the inputs and recorded in OP-SYS-035: how the rule-defined fault event is made observable in a test build or on the simulator, the common time base and its resolution, and how a test sets the status signal low before the event while the start-up checks have passed (SYS-SAFE-006 drives it high in normal operation) and requests it high after the event.

items.text: When the safe state is latched under SYS-RST-003 or SYS-RST-004, the controller shall keep the status signal low without interruption from the reset that preceded the latching until the next power-on reset, across every software reset and watchdog reset in between.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-009 for F-sys-req-item-r2-020; the status-signal counterpart of SYS-SAFE-010. The hold interval and its exit are stated by events independent of the signal levels. (1) Entry: the reset that preceded the latching. For a configuration-range fault that is the reset before the start-up range check that detected it (SYS-CFG-008, SYS-RST-003); for repeated faults it is the third consecutive supervisor reset with the same fault code (SYS-RST-004, CON-SUP-110). The status signal is already held low from that reset (SYS-SAFE-005, SYS-SAFE-008), so no transition is needed at latching. (2) Exit: the next power-on reset. CON-SUP-110 latches the safe state until a power-on reset and keeps the latch across software and watchdog resets (SYS-RST-005); STK-SUP-010 requires staying in the safe state until power-cycled. A software or watchdog reset while latched, including the recurring watchdog resets of OP-SYS-010, does not end the interval; after such a reset the start-up checks can pass again, but SYS-SAFE-006 drives the status signal high only when the safe state is not latched, and this item keeps it low. After a power-on reset the latch is cleared (SYS-RST-007) and SYS-SAFE-005 and SYS-SAFE-006 apply. (3) Not given by the inputs: whether a reset classified as 'other' (CON-SUP-111) keeps the latch or counts as a power-on reset, recorded in OP-SYS-024, and which reset flags identify a power-on reset, OP-SYS-016. The feasibility of holding the status signal low while a reset is asserted and before software can act, and whether the simulator models that interval, are OP-SYS-019; the hardware allocation covers that interval. Verification: latch the safe state by a configuration-range fault and, separately, by three same-code supervisor resets (test hooks, CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002); while latched, apply on the simulator (CON-SUP-005) a software reset, an independent-watchdog reset and a window-watchdog reset, in the repeated-fault case with a valid code image and configuration data block so that the start-up checks pass after each of them; record the status signal from the reset preceding the latching until a power-on reset and check that it is not high at any sample, across each of those resets; then apply a power-on reset with a valid code image and configuration data block and check that the latch is cleared and that the status signal is driven high when the start-up checks have passed (SYS-SAFE-006). Status open: OP-SYS-024 (exit by an 'other' reset) and OP-SYS-041 (functions active when the start-up checks pass while latched).

items.text: From any reset until the start-up checks have passed, the controller shall hold both control outputs low.
items.rationale: The obligation is taken unchanged from the product decision CON-SUP-109. Its feasibility is not established by the inputs: CON-SUP-003 only makes GPIO available for the control outputs, and no input gives the output pin levels while a reset is asserted or between reset release and the first instant software can drive the pins, for any reset path, nor any board circuit that holds the levels in that interval. The analysis needed per reset path, and the limit of the verification platform for that interval, are recorded in OP-SYS-018. The hardware allocation covers the interval before supervisor code can act; the software allocation covers the interval from then until the start-up checks have passed.

items.text: From any reset until the start-up checks have passed, the controller shall hold the status signal low.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-020. The obligation is taken unchanged from the product decision CON-SUP-109; it is the status-signal counterpart of SYS-SAFE-004. Its feasibility is not established by the inputs: CON-SUP-003 only makes GPIO available for the status signal, and no input gives the external level of the status-signal pin while a reset is asserted or between reset release and the first instant software can drive it, for any reset path, nor any board circuit that holds the level low in that interval. This matters in particular for resets taken while the controller is operational (status signal high, SYS-SAFE-006), such as a supervisor software reset or a watchdog reset, where a level kept from before the reset would show 'operational' during start-up, and for an undriven pin, whose level an observer cannot read as 'not operational'. The feasibility analysis needed per reset path, and the limit of the verification platform for that interval, are recorded in OP-SYS-019; the control-output analysis is OP-SYS-018. The hardware allocation covers the interval before supervisor code can act; the software allocation covers the interval from then until the start-up checks have passed.

items.text: When the start-up checks have passed while the safe state is not latched, the controller shall drive the status signal high.
When the independent watchdog, which runs from a clock of its own, has not been refreshed for 100 ms, the controller shall undergo a hardware reset.
When the window watchdog is refreshed earlier than 6 ms after its previous refresh, the controller shall undergo a hardware reset.
items.rationale: Split in rework (F-sys-req-item-r1-021): this item keeps the lower window limit of CON-SUP-106. Expiry of the upper limit of 12 ms, including when no later refresh is attempted, is SYS-WDG-006.

items.text: While no alive, late-start, overrun or program-flow fault has become detectable since the latest reset, the controller shall refresh the window watchdog once at the end of each control cycle, after the program-flow check of that control cycle has completed, where a fault becomes detectable at the instant that CON-SUP-105 gives for its rule: an alive fault at the end of its alive window under SYS-SUP-001, a late-start fault at the expiry of the start limit of the late release under SYS-SUP-002, an overrun fault at the expiry of the execution limit of the overrunning release under SYS-SUP-003, and a program-flow fault at the end of the control cycle for which SYS-SUP-005 detects it, and a fault that becomes detectable at the instant of a refresh has become detectable at that refresh.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-019 and F-sys-req-item-r3-020 (earlier F-sys-req-item-r2-033, F-sys-req-item-r1-022). (1) One refresh cutoff (F-sys-req-item-r3-019): the cutoff for STK-SUP-005 is the detectability instant of CON-SUP-105, defined in the text for each fault class. It is used for both sides of the rule: this item requires the refresh only while no fault has become detectable, and SYS-WDG-007 (split from this item) forbids every window-watchdog refresh from that same instant, inclusive, until the next reset. A detectability instant equal to the refresh instant ends the obligation and starts the prohibition, so no instant exists at which a refresh is both required and forbidden, or neither required nor forbidden. The former rationale stated the prohibition from detectability while the text left the prohibition to SYS-WDG-005, which counts from the detection (declaration); SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-003 place the declaration at or after the expiry of the limit, with a latency open in OP-SYS-025 and OP-SYS-026, so between the two events a refresh was neither required nor forbidden. The detectability instant is chosen, not the declaration, because it is the only fault instant the inputs define (CON-SUP-105) and because from it the task is no longer healthy in the sense of STK-SUP-005; a cutoff at the declaration would let refreshes continue for an undecided latency after a limit has expired. For F-sys-req-set-r1-007, SYS-WDG-004 and SYS-WDG-005 now use the same detectability instant for the independent watchdog, and SYS-WDG-005 no longer covers the window watchdog. (2) Faults identified by their rule: the detectability instant belongs to a fault that its rule gives (a missed alive window under SYS-SUP-001, a release that is late under SYS-SUP-002, a release that overruns under SYS-SUP-003, a flow fault of a cycle under SYS-SUP-005), so it is fixed on the time line whether or not the declaration has yet occurred. For a pending release, lateness is decided by the measured elapsed time, which can remain equal to the start limit for up to 100 µs after the expiry depending on the mapping and alignment of the measurement steps (OP-SYS-027); a refresh inside that interval is required or forbidden depending on whether the task then begins before the measured value exceeds the limit. The OP-SYS-027 decision resolves this; no new open point is raised. The overrun expiry depends on the execution-time measure open in OP-SYS-013 (d). (3) Position of each cutoff relative to the refresh: the refresh follows the completion of the flow check of its cycle (CON-SUP-104, CON-SUP-106); a flow fault becomes detectable at the end of that cycle and so withholds that refresh. An alive window ends at a control-cycle boundary (SYS-SUP-001), which is the end of the preceding control cycle, so an alive fault becomes detectable at the boundary that precedes the refresh of that cycle and withholds it. Only a late-start or overrun fault can become detectable strictly between the end of a cycle and its refresh. No input gives the interval from the end of the control cycle to the refresh; it consumes part of the 6 ms to 12 ms window of CON-SUP-106 and is part of the supervisor execution open in OP-SYS-013 (b). Interaction with the fault reaction sequence: OP-SYS-004; watchdog behaviour during the start-up checks and in the latched safe state: OP-SYS-010. Verification (reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-020): on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with a test build and the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002). In every run record on one virtual time base the end B_k of every control cycle k, the completion of each cycle's program-flow check, every window-watchdog refresh, the release and begin instants of every supervised task, the rule-defined event at which each late-start, overrun, alive or program-flow fault becomes detectable (not the fault report, whose <ms since start> field has millisecond resolution, SYS-DIAG-005), and the next reset. (V1) Fault-free, default configuration, at least 20 consecutive control cycles, which include two releases of T_DIAG (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-084): for each control cycle k record B_k, the completion F_k of its program-flow check and its refresh R_k. Pass if, for every k: (i) exactly one refresh R_k lies between B_k and B_(k+1); (ii) F_k is at or after B_k and is recorded before R_k, so the refresh follows the end of the cycle and the completion of its flow check; (iii) R_k - R_(k-1) is at least 6 ms and at most 12 ms (CON-SUP-106, SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006); (iv) the delays R_k - B_k meet SYS-WDG-008; (v) R_k - B_k is no more than the largest delay from the end of a control cycle to its refresh decided in OP-SYS-044, checked for each k independently of (iii) and (iv). A refresh before F_k, a cycle without a refresh or with two, a spacing outside 6 ms to 12 ms, or a delay R_k - B_k above the OP-SYS-044 limit fails. (V2) Alive fault at the coincident cycle boundary (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-014): with the alive hook, apply the isolating stimulus proposed in SYS-TEST-015 and awaiting approval in OP-SYS-038: from an injection instant inside control cycle N-2, after the T_IN completion of that cycle, alive supervision receives no completion of T_IN, while the releases, starts, executions, checkpoints and completions of T_IN seen by the timing and program-flow rules continue unchanged; alive supervision then counts no T_IN completion in control cycles N-1 and N, and the alive window of T_IN ends at B_N (SYS-SUP-001). Suppressing the releases of T_IN is not an isolating stimulus: each suppressed scheduled release leaves its checkpoint not arrived, so SYS-SUP-005 detects a program-flow fault at B_(N-1), which withholds the refresh after B_(N-1) before the alive rule acts. Validity, as evidence that the alive rule alone makes the refresh after B_N ineligible: the record shows (a) the injection instant after the T_IN completion of cycle N-2 and at or before B_(N-2); (b) a release, start, checkpoint receipt and completion of T_IN within its limits in each of cycles N-1 and N; (c) no T_IN completion counted by alive supervision in cycles N-1 and N; (d) no late-start, overrun or program-flow fault of any task, no alive fault of another task and no reset from the injection instant up to the latest refresh instant after B_N allowed by (V1) (v) (OP-SYS-044); and (e) the alive declaration for T_IN for the window ending at B_N. A run that does not show (a) to (e) is invalid, not passed. Pass: the refresh after B_(N-1) occurs, because the alive fault is not yet detectable there, and no refresh occurs at or after B_N until the next reset. If OP-SYS-038 approves no isolating stimulus, V2 is reported as not run, not passed; a stimulus approved there in place of the proposed one is used with the same validity criteria. (V3) Timing fault between the cycle boundary and the refresh, as a pair of runs with the same build and the same test configuration except the configured start limit of one supervised task X, where X has a release r in control cycle N+1 with B_N <= r and r earlier than the refresh after B_N, so that the held release has no checkpoint assigned to cycle N. In both runs the late-start hook holds that release of X unstarted until the next reset, so the release is late under SYS-SUP-002 and its detectability instant is E = r plus the configured start limit. Run P2: a start limit L2 with E2 = r + L2 later than the refresh after B_N; record that refresh instant R. Run P1: a start limit L1 with B_N < r + L1 < R. Validity: the record shows the same B_N, the same r and the same refresh instants up to and including the refresh after B_(N-1) in both runs, and no other fault becomes detectable at or before R in P2 or at or before E1 in P1. Pass: in P2 the refresh at R occurs and no refresh occurs at or after E2 until the next reset; in P1 no refresh occurs after B_N until the next reset. P1 shows that a fault that becomes detectable after the cycle boundary withholds the refresh of that cycle; P2 shows that the obligation holds up to the cutoff. (V4) Flow fault: with the program-flow hook withhold a checkpoint in cycle N; pass if no refresh occurs at or after B_N until the next reset and, if no other reset occurs first, a window-watchdog reset occurs after more than 12 ms have elapsed since the previous refresh and no later than the latest reset instant of OP-SYS-045 (SYS-WDG-006). Limits of V3: release instants inside the cycle are open in OP-SYS-013 (d) and the allowed granularity of a configured start limit in OP-SYS-028. If no supervised task has a release in the interval from B_N to R, or no admissible start limit places E1 between B_N and R, V3 cannot be built with a late-start fault; it may then use the overrun hook on a task executing across B_N with its execution-limit expiry placed between B_N and R, only if the measure decided in OP-SYS-013 (d) advances during that interval and the checkpoint of that task does not make cycle N faulty (OP-SYS-021). If neither can be built, V3 is reported as not run, not passed. The means by which control-cycle ends, flow-check completions, refreshes, release and begin instants and the rule-defined fault event are observed are not given by the inputs; they are the capabilities open in OP-SYS-037 and OP-SYS-034 (a) and (b), and they do not change this item. Status open: OP-SYS-004, OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-041 (refresh obligations during start-up, in the fault reaction and while latched). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-067: CON-SUP-106 requires the refresh of each control cycle at its end, and (iii) and SYS-WDG-008 only bound the spacing and the change of delay, so a steady delay of 9 ms passed them. Criterion (v) bounds the delay from each cycle end to its refresh directly and is checked separately from the inter-refresh spacing (iii). No input gives the largest delay at which a refresh still counts as made at the end of the cycle; it is recorded in OP-SYS-044 (blocking), and this item stays open until it is decided.

items.text: From the first instant after the latest reset at which an alive, late-start, overrun or program-flow fault becomes detectable as defined in SYS-WDG-003, including that instant, the controller shall not refresh the window watchdog until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-WDG-003 for F-sys-req-item-r3-019. This item is the prohibition side of the single refresh cutoff for STK-SUP-005: it counts from the same detectability instant (CON-SUP-105) that ends the refresh obligation of SYS-WDG-003, inclusive, so that eligibility and prohibition meet at one instant and no interval is left in which a refresh is neither required nor forbidden. SYS-WDG-005 states the same cutoff for the independent watchdog (F-sys-req-set-r1-007). Every fault is declared at or after its detectability instant (SYS-SUP-001, SYS-SUP-002, SYS-SUP-003, SYS-SUP-005), so the cutoff also covers the interval between detectability and declaration. Stopping the refresh leads to a window-watchdog reset once more than 12 ms have elapsed since the previous refresh and no later than the latest reset instant of OP-SYS-045 (SYS-WDG-006, reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-008); its conflict with the fault report and the supervisor software reset is OP-SYS-004 (blocking), as for SYS-WDG-005, so this item stays open until that is decided. The overrun expiry depends on the execution-time measure open in OP-SYS-013 (d), and the late-start decision in the up to 100 µs after the expiry of a start limit on OP-SYS-027. Verification: in the fault runs V2, V3 (P1 and P2) and V4 of SYS-WDG-003, and in one additional run in which the overrun hook (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002) keeps a supervised task executing past its execution limit, record on the Renode simulator's virtual time base (CON-SUP-005) the rule-defined event at which each fault becomes detectable (not the fault report, SYS-DIAG-005), every window-watchdog refresh and the next reset. Let E be the earliest such instant in the run. Pass: no refresh lies in the interval from E, inclusive, to the next reset. Where the declaration instant is also observed (OP-SYS-025 (c), OP-SYS-026 (b)) and lies after E, the same record confirms that no refresh occurs between E and the declaration. Coincident cutoff (added for F-sys-req-set-r1-086): the prohibition includes a refresh at the cutoff instant itself, which V3 does not exercise because it places E strictly before or after the reference refresh. (V5) With the build and test configuration of run P2 of SYS-WDG-003, whose record gives the refresh instant R after B_N, run P0 with a start limit L0 such that E0 = r + L0 equals R on the virtual time base, all else equal; the run is valid only if its record up to R matches P2, so that a refresh would otherwise fall at R. Pass: no refresh at R and none after it until the next reset; a refresh at R fails. Run P2, in which E lies after R and the refresh at R occurs, is the neighbouring case, so the pair distinguishes a refresh at the cutoff from one immediately before it. If no admissible start limit places E0 exactly at R (granularity of configured limits, OP-SYS-028; time-base resolution, OP-SYS-037), V5 is replaced by an analysis of the detailed design showing that the refresh decision treats a fault whose detectability instant equals the refresh instant as detectable, supported by host unit tests (CON-SUP-005) of that decision with equal time values, and the test form is reported as not run. The observation means are not given by the inputs; they are the capabilities open in OP-SYS-037 and OP-SYS-034 (a) and (b).

items.text: While no alive, late-start, overrun or program-flow fault has become detectable since the latest reset as defined in SYS-WDG-003, the controller shall refresh the independent watchdog at intervals shorter than 100 ms.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-007. STK-SUP-005 allows service of both watchdogs only while every supervised task is healthy. The independent watchdog now uses the same health transition as the window watchdog (SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-007): the detectability instant of CON-SUP-105, defined per fault class in SYS-WDG-003, not the later declaration of the fault. The obligation ends, and the prohibition of SYS-WDG-005 starts, at that instant, inclusive, so no independent-watchdog refresh is required after the set treats the task as unhealthy, and no instant has a refresh both required and forbidden. 'Shorter than 100 ms' follows the 100 ms timeout of CON-SUP-106 (SYS-WDG-001): an interval of exactly 100 ms does not conform (SYS-TEST-013). Status open: watchdog behaviour during the start-up checks and in the latched safe state, OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-041; interaction with the fault reaction sequence, OP-SYS-004.

items.text: From the first instant after the latest reset at which an alive, late-start, overrun or program-flow fault becomes detectable as defined in SYS-WDG-003, including that instant, the controller shall not refresh the independent watchdog until the next reset.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-007. States the 'only while every supervised task is healthy' part of STK-SUP-005 for the independent watchdog, with the same health transition and the same inclusive cutoff as SYS-WDG-007 for the window watchdog. The former text counted from the detection (declaration) of the fault, which SYS-SUP-002 and SYS-SUP-003 place at or after the detectability instant, so a pending declaration could leave an independent-watchdog refresh required after the set already treated the task as unhealthy for the window watchdog. The window-watchdog prohibition is SYS-WDG-007 and is no longer repeated here. Stopping the refresh leads to an independent-watchdog reset 100 ms after the last refresh (SYS-WDG-001). See OP-SYS-004 for the conflict with the fault report and software reset deadlines. Verification: in the fault runs of SYS-WDG-007, record also every independent-watchdog refresh; pass if no independent-watchdog refresh lies in the interval from E, inclusive, to the next reset.

items.text: When more than 12 ms have elapsed since the previous refresh of the window watchdog without a further refresh, the controller shall undergo a hardware reset no later than the latest reset instant after the previous refresh decided in OP-SYS-045.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-WDG-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-021). States the upper window limit of CON-SUP-106 as an expiry, so the reset occurs both when refreshes cease entirely (the case STK-SUP-005 relies on: a failure the software does not handle still ends in a hardware reset) and when a refresh is attempted later than 12 ms. The window-watchdog register values that realise the 12 ms limit are set in the design from the reference manual (CON-SUP-106). Precedence of this reset over the fault report and supervisor reset is OP-SYS-004; watchdog behaviour before the first refresh after reset is OP-SYS-010. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-009. CON-SUP-106 makes only a refresh later than 12 ms after the previous refresh invalid, so a refresh exactly 12 ms after the previous one is valid and causes no reset: at that boundary the refresh takes precedence over the expiry, and the window expires only when more than 12 ms have elapsed without a further refresh. The same boundary is used in SYS-WDG-003 (V1), SYS-WDG-008 and SYS-TEST-012, which accept a spacing of exactly 12 ms, and the lower limit of SYS-WDG-002 likewise accepts a refresh exactly 6 ms after the previous one. A window realised in the design whose upper limit is below 12 ms would reset on a valid refresh and does not conform. Verification on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002): (W1) refresh exactly 12 ms after the previous refresh on the virtual time base; pass if no window-watchdog reset occurs at or before that refresh or because of it; (W2) stop refreshing; pass if a window-watchdog reset occurs after more than 12 ms have elapsed since the last refresh, not at or before 12 ms, and no later than the latest reset instant decided in OP-SYS-045, measured from the last refresh on the virtual time base; the criterion is fixed at system level and not delegated to the limit that the design realises. Placing a refresh at a given virtual instant and the simulator's modelling of the window-watchdog timing are capabilities of the verification environment that the inputs do not state (OP-SYS-037). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-008 and F-sys-req-set-r2-011. Common no-refresh criterion: the window expires once more than 12 ms have elapsed since the previous refresh, a refresh at exactly 12 ms stays valid (W1), and the reset occurs no later than the latest reset instant of OP-SYS-045. CON-SUP-106 gives the 12 ms limit but no tolerance between expiry and reset, and a hardware window watchdog counts in discrete steps, so the latest reset instant needs approval (OP-SYS-045, blocking). The same criterion is used in SYS-WDG-003 (V4), SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-SUP-009. Status set to open: the latest reset instant is undecided (OP-SYS-045), and the behaviour before the first refresh after reset, which decides from when this item applies, is the blocking OP-SYS-010.

items.text: For each pair of consecutive control cycles in which SYS-WDG-003 requires a window-watchdog refresh, the controller shall make the delay from the end of the later control cycle to its refresh no more than 2 ms longer and no more than 4 ms shorter than the delay from the end of the earlier control cycle to its refresh.
items.rationale: Derived for F-sys-req-set-r1-011 from CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-106. Under SYS-WDG-003 the refresh of control cycle k follows the end B_k of that cycle and the completion of its program-flow check, after a delay d_k. Control-cycle ends are 10 ms apart (CON-SUP-101), so the interval between consecutive refreshes is 10 ms + (d_(k+1) - d_k). CON-SUP-106 limits that interval to 6 ms to 12 ms, both included (SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006), so d_(k+1) - d_k must lie from -4 ms to +2 ms. This item states that relation for the refreshes the controller makes in fault-free operation, which no other item states; SYS-WDG-002 and SYS-WDG-006 state only the hardware reaction. A sufficient design criterion is that every d_k lies within one range at most 2 ms wide. The delay consists of the end-of-cycle program-flow check, any other supervisor work placed before the refresh, and interference from interrupts and from tasks executing across the cycle end (for example T_DIAG, whose 20 ms execution limit exceeds the control cycle). None of these is bounded by the inputs: their bounds are the evidence requested in OP-SYS-013 (b), (c) and (d), so the feasibility of this item is not established and it stays open until OP-SYS-013 is decided. Any variation of the cycle ends around the 10 ms grid (time-base interrupt latency, OP-SYS-013 (c)) adds to d_(k+1) - d_k and is included in the analysis. The first refresh after the start-up checks and refreshes in the latched safe state are OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-041. Verification (analysis): from the software architecture and detailed design, determine the minimum and maximum delay from the end of a control cycle to its refresh under the configured schedule, including the program-flow check, interrupt load and preemption by or of supervised tasks. Pass if the maximum minus the minimum is at most 2 ms or, failing that, if every admissible pair of consecutive delays meets the stated relation. Supporting evidence: run V1 of SYS-WDG-003 and SYS-TEST-012, which record every cycle end and refresh; it supports the analysis and does not replace it. The bound on each single delay from the end of a control cycle to its refresh is OP-SYS-044 (F-sys-req-set-r2-067), checked in SYS-WDG-003 (V1) (v); this item limits only the change of delay between consecutive cycles.

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault while the safe state is not latched and no such fault has been detected earlier since the latest reset, the controller shall request a software reset within 20 ms of the safe-state entry instant of that fault defined in SYS-RST-002.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-008. The 20 ms of CON-SUP-110 counts from safe-state entry. The former origin, 'the instant at which both control outputs and the status signal are low', describes an interval when they are already low at detection; the origin is now the safe-state entry instant that SYS-RST-002 defines for each fault: the detection instant of CON-SUP-105 if both control outputs and the status signal are low at that instant, otherwise the first later instant at which they are all low. The item applies to the first such fault after the latest reset. Whether a later fault detected before the reset request moves the deadline, and whether its report must also be transmitted first, are left to the decision in OP-SYS-033 and are not stated here. Faults detected during the start-up checks, when CON-SUP-109 already holds the outputs low, are covered by SYS-RST-012. Configuration-range faults latch instead (SYS-RST-003, CON-SUP-115). A reset requested by the supervisor is a 'supervisor reset' in this set. See OP-SYS-004, OP-SYS-009 and OP-SYS-041. For F-sys-req-set-r2-004: the fault whose entry instant starts this deadline is the fault whose code SYS-RST-004 attributes to the resulting supervisor reset.

items.text: When a start-up code-integrity or configuration-integrity fault is detected while the safe state is not latched, the controller shall request a software reset within 20 ms of the completion of the failing integrity computation.
items.rationale: Status open for OP-SYS-040 (F-sys-req-set-r1-002): when the configuration-integrity check fails and a range violation is also observed in the same block, the inputs do not say whether this item (software reset, code 6) or SYS-RST-003 (latch, code 9) applies. Split from SYS-RST-001. From any reset until the start-up checks pass, CON-SUP-109 (SYS-SAFE-004, SYS-SAFE-005) already holds both control outputs and the status signal low, so the safe-state condition of SYS-SAFE-003 is met at the detection instant and no output transition marks safe-state entry. Safe-state entry for these faults is therefore the detection instant of CON-SUP-105 (completion of the failing integrity computation), which is the origin of the 20 ms of CON-SUP-110. Configuration-range faults detected at start-up latch instead (SYS-RST-003). The fault report precedes the reset request (SYS-RST-002). See OP-SYS-009 and OP-SYS-010.

items.text: When the controller detects an alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault while the safe state is not latched, the controller shall start the transmission of the fault report of that fault on the diagnostic serial line no earlier than the safe-state entry instant of that fault, which is the detection instant defined in CON-SUP-105 if both control outputs and the status signal are low at that instant, and otherwise the first instant after the detection instant at which both control outputs and the status signal are low.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-028, F-sys-req-item-r2-010 and F-sys-req-item-r3-005, and split. CON-SUP-110 orders the fault reaction as safe-state entry, then fault-report transmission, then the software reset request. This item fixes the first step for the faults of SYS-RST-001 (detected after the start-up checks have passed). The safe-state entry instant is defined for every fault, so each fault has a distinct entry event: (a) when both control outputs and the status signal are still high or partly high at detection, it is the first later instant at which SYS-SAFE-001 and SYS-SAFE-002 are both met; (b) when they become low at the detection instant itself, or (c) when they are already low because an earlier fault has already put the controller in the safe state and no reset has yet followed, the controller is in the safe state at detection, so the entry instant is the detection instant of CON-SUP-105. Case (c) follows the rule SYS-RST-012 already applies when CON-SUP-109 holds the outputs low at detection. The trigger is the detection of the fault rather than the reset request, so a second fault detected before the reset is covered. SYS-RST-001 now counts its reset deadline from this entry instant (F-sys-req-set-r1-008); the undecided reaction to a second fault detected in the safe state is OP-SYS-033. For start-up code-integrity and configuration-integrity faults, where CON-SUP-109 already holds the outputs low, the reference is the start-up entry event of SYS-RST-012 and is stated in SYS-RST-014. SYS-RST-013 fixes the second step: transmission completes before the reset request. Configuration-range faults latch instead (SYS-RST-003), and a watchdog-reset fault has no safe-state reaction (SYS-RST-011). Together with SYS-DIAG-002 (report within 10 ms of detection), this ordering requires safe-state entry early enough for the report to fit inside the 10 ms. The reading of 'sent' in CON-SUP-112 is OP-SYS-007. Whether a window-watchdog reset can preempt the transmission (F-sys-req-item-r1-029) remains OP-SYS-004.

items.text: When a start-up code-integrity or configuration-integrity fault causes the controller to request a software reset, the controller shall start the transmission of the fault report of that fault on the diagnostic serial line no earlier than the completion of the failing integrity computation.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-RST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r2-010). From any reset until the start-up checks pass, CON-SUP-109 already holds both control outputs and the status signal low, so no output transition marks safe-state entry for these faults. As stated in SYS-RST-012, safe-state entry for them is the completion of the failing integrity computation (the detection instant of CON-SUP-105), which is the reference for the CON-SUP-110 order (safe-state entry, then fault-report transmission, then software reset request). SYS-RST-013 requires the transmission to complete before the reset request. Configuration-range faults latch instead (SYS-RST-003). The reading of 'sent' in CON-SUP-112 is OP-SYS-007. Whether a window-watchdog reset can preempt the transmission remains OP-SYS-004.

items.text: When a fault causes the controller to request a software reset, the controller shall complete the transmission of the fault report of that fault on the diagnostic serial line, including its terminating line feed, before requesting the software reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-RST-002 (F-sys-req-item-r1-028). This item is the second step of the CON-SUP-110 sequence (safe-state entry, then fault-report transmission, then software reset request). SYS-RST-002 states when transmission may start. SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-012 state the deadline for the reset request. Whether the report can complete before a window-watchdog reset once refreshes stop (SYS-WDG-005) is unresolved: see OP-SYS-004. For F-sys-req-set-r2-004: the fault that causes the reset request is the fault attributed to that reset in SYS-RST-004 (the fault whose safe-state entry starts the deadline of SYS-RST-001, or the start-up fault of SYS-RST-012). Whether the report of a later fault detected before the reset must also be completed is OP-SYS-033 (a).

items.text: When a configuration-range fault is detected, the controller shall latch the safe state until the next power-on reset.
items.rationale: Status open: OP-SYS-040 (validity and precedence when a configuration-integrity failure and a configuration-range violation are both observed, F-sys-req-set-r1-002), OP-SYS-041 (functions active when the start-up checks pass while latched), OP-SYS-024 (exit by an 'other' reset) and OP-SYS-010 (watchdogs in the latched safe state).

items.text: When the controller starts after the third consecutive supervisor reset with the same fault code, with no interval of 60 s of fault-free operation between the first and the third of those resets, the controller shall latch the safe state until the next power-on reset, where the fault code of a supervisor reset is the fault code of the fault whose safe-state entry instant starts the reset deadline of SYS-RST-001, or of the fault that causes the software reset request of SYS-RST-012, and not the code of any later fault detected before that reset.
items.rationale: Status open for OP-SYS-041 (F-sys-req-set-r1-003): which application and supervisor functions are active when the start-up checks pass while the safe state is latched is not given by the inputs. 'Same fault' means same fault code (CON-SUP-110). 'Fault-free operation' is operation after the start-up checks have passed with no fault detected. How other resets or other fault codes between those resets affect the count is not given (OP-SYS-006). Retention of the reset-sequence state across software and watchdog resets, including a reset during its update, is open in OP-SYS-043 (F-sys-req-set-r1-012). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-004 (fault code attributed to a supervisor reset). CON-SUP-110 orders the reaction as entry into the safe state, then the fault report, then the software reset request, so the reset follows the fault that entered the safe state. A fault detected while the controller is already in the safe state does not enter it (SYS-RST-002 case (c)) and does not start a new reset deadline in SYS-RST-001. The attributed code is therefore that of the first alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault since the latest reset (SYS-RST-001), or of the start-up integrity fault (SYS-RST-012). This reading is taken from the order of CON-SUP-110 and is not an approved rule; its confirmation is added to OP-SYS-033 as point (c), so that the count at the next start-up does not depend on an implementation choice. Mixed-code verification on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) with the test hooks (CON-SUP-116, SYS-TEST-002): in each run, before each of three supervisor resets inject a first fault A and, after its safe-state entry and before the reset request, a second fault B of another code, with less than 60 s of fault-free operation between the first and the third reset and no other reset in between. Record the codes of A and B, the fault reports, every reset and its classified cause, and the latch state at each start-up. (M1) A has code 1 before all three resets; B has code 3, then 2, then 3. Pass: the safe state is latched at the start-up after the third reset. (M2) A has code 1, then 3, then 1; B has code 3, then 1, then 3. Pass: the safe state is not latched at the start-up after the third reset. M1 fails a rule that attributes the code of the last fault; M2 fails a rule that counts every code reported before a reset. The outcome of M2 does not depend on OP-SYS-006, because no attributed code occurs at all three resets. A run with a window-watchdog reset instead of a supervisor reset (OP-SYS-004) is invalid, not passed.

items.text: The controller shall retain the safe-state latch across software resets and watchdog resets.
items.rationale: Retention depends on platform and simulator capabilities that the inputs do not establish (which memory of the device survives each reset kind, start-up code that leaves it uninitialised, the Renode model, and a reset during an update of the latch); these and the evidence method for each are recorded in OP-SYS-043 (F-sys-req-set-r1-012). Status open until it is decided; see also OP-SYS-024.

items.text: The controller shall retain the fault history across software resets and watchdog resets.
items.rationale: Retention depends on platform and simulator capabilities that the inputs do not establish (which memory of the device survives each reset kind, start-up code that leaves it uninitialised, the Renode model, and a reset during an update of the history); these and the evidence method for each are recorded in OP-SYS-043 (F-sys-req-set-r1-012). Status open until it is decided.

items.text: After a power-on reset, the controller shall start with the safe-state latch cleared.
items.rationale: Status open: identification of a power-on reset (OP-SYS-016), the latch after 'other' resets (OP-SYS-024) and clearing of the reset-surviving memory on power loss (OP-SYS-043).

items.text: At start-up, the controller shall classify the cause of the preceding reset, on the basis of the hardware reset flags, as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor (software) reset or other.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r1-031 and F-sys-req-item-r2-011. CON-SUP-111 makes the reset flags the basis of the classification and CON-SUP-003 places them in the RCC. The round-2 restriction 'and from no other evidence' had no basis in the inputs and is removed. The inputs do not say whether the flags alone distinguish a supervisor (software) reset from another software-requested reset, nor whether corroborating evidence (for example data kept in reset-surviving memory, CON-SUP-110) may or must be used; this is recorded in OP-SYS-023 and is not decided here. Verification sets each reset-flag pattern, for example by injecting each reset kind on the simulator (CON-SUP-005, CON-SUP-116), and checks that the class follows the flags. The inputs do not give the mapping from flag patterns to the five classes. That mapping, which class applies when several flags are set, and whether flags from earlier resets persist until cleared, are open in OP-SYS-016. Flag meanings are hardware facts to be cited from RM0486 (CON-SUP-002) by section and page; they are not assumed here.

items.text: At start-up, the controller shall transmit a start-up message carrying the classified reset cause on the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: The content and format of the start-up message are not given (OP-SYS-002).

items.text: The controller shall make the classified cause of the latest reset readable by the service tool over the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: No service request defined in CON-SUP-113 returns the reset cause (OP-SYS-002).

items.text: When the reset cause classified at start-up is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the controller shall detect a watchdog-reset fault.
items.rationale: The watchdog-reset fault is reported like every detected fault (SYS-DIAG-002, fault code per SYS-DIAG-003). Its entity field is not given (OP-SYS-003). Status open: OP-SYS-003 and OP-SYS-016.

items.text: The diagnostic serial line shall operate at 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

When the controller detects a fault, the controller shall transmit on the diagnostic serial line, within 10 ms of the detection instant, one fault report line of the form FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed.
items.rationale: 'Within 10 ms' is read as the line feed having been transmitted, the stricter reading of 'sent' in CON-SUP-112 (OP-SYS-007). Serial-line load (F-sys-req-set-r1-004): the diagnostic serial line (CON-SUP-007) carries the start-up message (SYS-RST-009), fault reports (this item) and the answers to GET STATUS, GET FAULTS and other requests (SYS-DIAG-007 to SYS-DIAG-009). At 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit, one character takes 10 bit times, 86.8 µs. A fault report line has 14 characters plus the digits of <ms since start>: 4 for FLT and its comma, 1 code digit, 1 comma, at most 6 entity characters (T_CTRL, T_DIAG or CONFIG), 1 comma and 1 line feed. No input bounds the number of digits of <ms since start>; with 10 digits a report has 24 characters and takes 2.08 ms. A GET FAULTS answer of 8 such reports takes 16.7 ms before the framing open in OP-SYS-001, so a fault report that becomes due during that answer cannot complete within 10 ms of detection if it waits for the end of the answer, and at most 4 reports of 24 characters fit back to back in 10 ms. The start-up message length is open (OP-SYS-002). These figures are arithmetic on CON-SUP-007 and CON-SUP-112, not a schedule. The permitted concurrent traffic, the frame-handling rules and the order and number of pending reports are not given by the inputs and are recorded in OP-SYS-042; this item stays open until they are decided, and also for OP-SYS-004, OP-SYS-007, OP-SYS-017, OP-SYS-033, OP-SYS-040 and OP-SYS-041.

items.text: The fault report shall carry fault code 1 for an alive fault, 2 for a late-start fault, 3 for an overrun fault, 4 for a program-flow fault, 5 for a start-up code-integrity fault, 6 for a configuration-integrity fault, 7 for a run-time code-integrity fault, 8 for a watchdog-reset fault and 9 for a configuration-range fault.

quality_waivers.rationale: The numbers are fault-code identifiers defined in CON-SUP-112, not physical quantities, so they carry no unit.

items.text: The fault report shall carry as entity the name of the affected supervised task for alive, late-start, overrun and program-flow faults, CODE for code-integrity faults, and CONFIG for configuration-integrity and configuration-range faults.
items.rationale: The entity for a watchdog-reset fault is not given (OP-SYS-003); the affected task of a program-flow fault is not defined (OP-SYS-008).

items.text: The <ms since start> field of a fault report shall state the detection instant in milliseconds elapsed since the controller started after its latest reset.
items.rationale: The start instant from which the time is counted is not given (OP-SYS-007); the detection instant of a configuration-range fault is not given (OP-SYS-017).

items.text: While fewer than 8 faults have been detected since the latest power-on reset, the controller shall hold in the fault history the fault reports of all faults detected since that power-on reset and no other fault report, whether or not the transmission of each report on the diagnostic serial line has completed.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-002 and split: this item fixes the history content before 8 faults have been detected; SYS-DIAG-011 fixes it from the eighth fault on, where the report of each newly detected fault displaces the report of the earliest detected fault held. CON-SUP-113 makes GET FAULTS (SYS-DIAG-008) return the last 8 fault reports, so the history holds no report older than those 8. CON-SUP-110 keeps the history across software and watchdog resets but not across power loss (SYS-RST-006), so the faults counted are those detected since the latest power-on reset. Whether other resets (for example an external pin or supply-level reset) keep the history, and the order among faults detected at the same instant, are open in OP-SYS-022. CON-SUP-113 and STK-SUP-013 put no condition on transmission and STK-SUP-012 gives one report per detected fault, so membership follows detection and a reset that interrupts a transmission does not remove the report. The instant of entry is stated in SYS-DIAG-010; a reset between detection and entry is open in OP-SYS-015. Verifiable by injecting 0 to 7 faults after a power-on reset (CON-SUP-116) and reading GET FAULTS. Status open: OP-SYS-015, OP-SYS-022 and OP-SYS-043.

items.text: While at least 8 faults have been detected since the latest power-on reset, the controller shall hold in the fault history the fault reports of the 8 most recently detected faults and no other fault report, whether or not the transmission of each report on the diagnostic serial line has completed.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-006 for F-sys-req-item-r2-002. CON-SUP-113 limits the history returned by GET FAULTS (SYS-DIAG-008) to the last 8 fault reports, so when a fault is detected while 8 reports are held, its report displaces the report of the earliest detected fault held. The count starts at the latest power-on reset because CON-SUP-110 keeps the history across software and watchdog resets but not across power loss (SYS-RST-006). Retention across other resets and the order among faults detected at the same instant are open in OP-SYS-022; a reset between detection and entry is open in OP-SYS-015. Verifiable by injecting 8, 9 and more faults after a power-on reset (CON-SUP-116) and reading GET FAULTS. Status open: OP-SYS-015, OP-SYS-022 and OP-SYS-043.

items.text: When the controller detects a fault, the controller shall complete the entry of the fault report of that fault in the fault history no later than the instant at which the first bit of that report is transmitted on the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: Derived: the inputs do not state when a report enters the history. Completing the entry by the time its transmission starts makes the report available to GET FAULTS after a software or watchdog reset that interrupts the transmission (CON-SUP-110 transmit-then-reset sequence; history retained across these resets, SYS-RST-006). A reset between detection and the start of transmission is not covered by this ordering; that case and confirmation of the entry instant are recorded in OP-SYS-015 (see also OP-SYS-004). Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-035: the end of the ordering is the first transmitted bit of the report. Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-002: strict precedence is not retained. CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-113 give no ordering at the first-bit boundary, and the purpose above needs only that the entry is complete when transmission starts. The ordering is therefore non-strict: an entry completed at the same instant as the first bit conforms, and an entry completed after that instant does not. Whether entry must strictly precede transmission is part of the entry-instant decision in OP-SYS-015. Test (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-057): reading the history after a restart alone cannot show the order, because start-up could rebuild a report from other retained data even if the history entry was incomplete at the first bit. (T1) Order: on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-005) inject a fault through a test hook (CON-SUP-116) and record on one common time base the instant at which the history entry of that report is complete in the reset-surviving memory (the last write of the entry, including any validity marker the design uses) and the instant at which the start bit of the first character of that report begins on the diagnostic serial line. Pass: the completion instant is not later than the first-bit instant; a later completion fails. Repeat for each fault class that can be injected after the start-up checks have passed and for one start-up integrity fault. (T2) Post-reset outcome, judged separately: in a separate run, apply a software reset or a watchdog reset at the first-bit instant before any further controller instruction executes, let the controller restart and send GET FAULTS (SYS-DIAG-008). Pass: the answer contains that fault report. T2 shows retention and availability after the reset (SYS-RST-006, CON-SUP-110), not the entry order, which T1 decides. Observing the completion of the durable entry, halting on the first transmitted bit and applying the reset at that instant are capabilities of the verification environment that the inputs do not state; they are recorded in OP-SYS-015 (c) and OP-SYS-043.

items.text: When the controller receives the service request GET STATUS on the diagnostic serial line, the controller shall answer STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms.
items.rationale: The values of <state>, the meaning of <fault count> and the request framing are not given (OP-SYS-001).

items.text: When the controller receives the service request GET FAULTS on the diagnostic serial line, the controller shall answer with the fault reports held in the fault history within 50 ms.
items.rationale: Order, framing and the answer when fewer than 8 reports are held are not given (OP-SYS-001). For F-sys-req-set-r2-009: a request completed after safe-state entry cannot be answered within the 50 ms in every case; the assessment of the service time left before the reset against the reply lengths, and the decision it frames, are in OP-SYS-009. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-010: the service time assessment in OP-SYS-009 is recalculated with the allowed fault report lengths of 13 to 24 characters (CON-SUP-007, CON-SUP-112); it states its assumptions on the latency from the end of the fault report to the reset request and from the request to the reset event, and judges a reply as cut off by the reset event (the reset taking effect), not by the reset request. The decision itself remains open in OP-SYS-009.

items.text: When the controller receives a service request other than GET STATUS or GET FAULTS on the diagnostic serial line, the controller shall answer ERR.
items.rationale: No answer time is given for ERR (OP-SYS-001).

items.text: In normal operation with no fault and no service request, the supervisor software shall use at most 10 % of the processor time in any 1 s window, measured on the simulator at the configured core clock.
items.rationale: The configured core clock value is not given (OP-SYS-012).

items.text: When the controller software is started on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, the controller shall transmit the start-up message of SYS-RST-009 on the simulated diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: Split in rework (F-sys-req-item-r2-032) into four observable outcomes on the simulator: the image loads and executes (this item, start-up message), the start-up checks pass (SYS-TEST-004), and supervised control cycles execute (SYS-TEST-005, SYS-TEST-006). The controller has no test-runner function; integration and system tests are executed by the verification environment on the Renode simulator (CON-SUP-116, CON-SUP-005). The start-up message format is open (OP-SYS-002), so the demonstration observes the presence of the message, not its content. Status set to open for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: the start-up message cannot be told apart from other output on the line until its format is decided (OP-SYS-002, blocking), and whether the watchdogs run during the start-up checks, which decides whether the message is reached before a watchdog timeout, is OP-SYS-010 (blocking).

items.text: When the controller software is started on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration, an intact program code image, an intact configuration data block, the safe state not latched and no fault injected, the controller shall drive the simulated status signal from low to high at an instant not earlier than the successful completion of each of the start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity and configuration-range checks, all recorded on one simulated time base.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-069: the nominal run now establishes the CON-SUP-109 ordering by itself. A status edge in this run and a status held low in the failure runs of SYS-TEST-007 to SYS-TEST-009 could all be observed if the valid path drove the status signal high before the checks finished and the failure paths suppressed the edge. The nominal run therefore records the successful completion of every start-up check (as in the valid-start test of SYS-MEM-004) and the status edge on one time base and compares their order; a run whose record lacks any of the three completions, or shows the edge before one of them, fails. SYS-TEST-007 to SYS-TEST-009 remain as failure-path evidence. Observation of the check completions: OP-SYS-030. Split from SYS-TEST-001 (F-sys-req-item-r2-032); reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-029 by a further split into SYS-TEST-004, SYS-TEST-007, SYS-TEST-008 and SYS-TEST-009. A high level observed in this nominal run alone does not show that the start-up checks have completed, because it would also appear if the controller drove the signal high before the checks finished. The link between the low-to-high transition and successful completion of the start-up checks (CON-SUP-109, SYS-SAFE-005, SYS-SAFE-006) is therefore demonstrated by this run together with SYS-TEST-007 (start-up code-integrity check, CON-SUP-107), SYS-TEST-008 (configuration-integrity check, CON-SUP-107) and SYS-TEST-009 (configuration-range check, CON-SUP-115), run on the same build. In each of those runs one start-up check fails, so a controller that drives the status signal high before that check completes shows a high level before the fault report line and fails the demonstration. The start-up evidence counts only when SYS-TEST-004, SYS-TEST-007, SYS-TEST-008 and SYS-TEST-009 all pass on that build. The feasibility of a low level before supervisor code executes is outside these demonstrations (OP-SYS-019).

items.text: When a test build of the controller software is started on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration in a configuration data block that passes the configuration-integrity and configuration-range checks, the safe state not latched and a start-up code-integrity fault injected through its fault-injection hook as the only injected fault, the controller shall transmit a complete fault report line with fault code 5 and entity CODE on the simulated diagnostic serial line while keeping the simulated status signal low without interruption from the start of execution of the controller software until the end of transmission of that line.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TEST-004 (F-sys-req-item-r3-029): the start-up code-integrity check fails in this run, so a high level before its fault report line shows that the status signal was driven high before the start-up checks completed, and fails the demonstration. Fault code 5 per CON-SUP-112; hook per SYS-TEST-002. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-072. Isolation: the configuration data block is a reference valid block (OP-SYS-005), so a configuration fault cannot hold the status signal low in place of the code-integrity case; the run is valid only if no fault report with code 6 or 9 is transmitted. Finite observation: from the start of execution until the next reset or, if none occurs, until a limit set from the maximum duration of the start-up checks, which no input gives (OP-SYS-010). Pass: a complete line FLT,5,CODE,<ms since start> with its line feed is received inside the observation, no later than 10 ms after the completion of the failing code-integrity computation (SYS-DIAG-002, CON-SUP-105; endpoint per OP-SYS-007) and before the software reset request (SYS-RST-013), and the status signal is low at every sample until the end of that line. A valid run whose observation ends without that complete line fails. Observation of the failing computation: OP-SYS-030. Status open: OP-SYS-005, OP-SYS-007 and OP-SYS-010.

quality_waivers.rationale: The number 5 is a fault-code identifier defined in CON-SUP-112 (SYS-DIAG-003), not a physical quantity, so it carries no unit.

items.text: When a test build of the controller software is started on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration, an intact program code image, the safe state not latched and a configuration-integrity fault injected through its fault-injection hook as the only injected fault, the controller shall transmit a complete fault report line with fault code 6 and entity CONFIG on the simulated diagnostic serial line while keeping the simulated status signal low without interruption from the start of execution of the controller software until the end of transmission of that line.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TEST-004 (F-sys-req-item-r3-029): the configuration-integrity check fails in this run, so a high level before its fault report line shows that the status signal was driven high before the start-up checks completed, and fails the demonstration. Fault code 6 per CON-SUP-112; hook per SYS-TEST-002. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-073. Isolation: the program code image is a reference intact image (OP-SYS-005), so a code-integrity failure cannot hold the status signal low in place of the configuration-integrity case; the run is valid only if no fault report with code 5 is transmitted. The injected fault changes content covered by the CRC without creating a CON-SUP-115 out-of-range value, because the outcome when both are observed is open (OP-SYS-040); a run with a code 9 report is invalid. Finite observation: from the start of execution until the next reset or, if none occurs, until a limit set from the maximum duration of the start-up checks (OP-SYS-010). Pass: a complete line FLT,6,CONFIG,<ms since start> with its line feed is received inside the observation, no later than 10 ms after the completion of the failing CRC computation (SYS-DIAG-002, CON-SUP-105; endpoint per OP-SYS-007) and before the software reset request (SYS-RST-013), and the status signal is low at every sample until the end of that line. A valid run whose observation ends without that complete line fails. Observation of the failing computation: OP-SYS-030. Status open: OP-SYS-005, OP-SYS-007, OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-040.

quality_waivers.rationale: The number 6 is a fault-code identifier defined in CON-SUP-112 (SYS-DIAG-003), not a physical quantity, so it carries no unit.

items.text: When a test build of the controller software is started on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with an intact program code image, the safe state not latched and a configuration-range fault injected through its fault-injection hook as the only injected fault, in a configuration data block whose stored CRC-32 matches its content, the controller shall transmit a complete fault report line with fault code 9 and entity CONFIG on the simulated diagnostic serial line while keeping the simulated status signal low without interruption from the start of execution of the controller software until the end of transmission of that line.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-TEST-004 (F-sys-req-item-r3-029): the configuration-range check fails in this run, so a high level before its fault report line shows that the status signal was driven high before the start-up checks completed, and fails the demonstration. Fault code 9 per CON-SUP-112 and CON-SUP-115; hook per SYS-TEST-002. Because a configuration-range fault latches the safe state (SYS-RST-003), this run is started after a power-on reset. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-074. Isolation: the stored CRC-32 is computed over the modified content with the interface decided in OP-SYS-005, so the configuration-integrity check passes, and the program code image is a reference intact image; the run is valid only if no fault report with code 5 or 6 is transmitted. Finite observation: a configuration-range fault latches the safe state (SYS-RST-003) and no software reset follows, so the observation ends 10 ms after the detectability instant of the configuration-range fault, which is open in OP-SYS-017, and until that is decided at a limit set from the maximum duration of the start-up checks (OP-SYS-010). Pass: a complete line FLT,9,CONFIG,<ms since start> with its line feed is received inside the observation, and the status signal is low at every sample until the end of that line. A valid run whose observation ends without that complete line fails. Status open: OP-SYS-005, OP-SYS-010 and OP-SYS-017.

quality_waivers.rationale: The number 9 is a fault-code identifier defined in CON-SUP-112 and CON-SUP-115 (SYS-DIAG-003), not a physical quantity, so it carries no unit.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, the controller shall keep the simulated status signal high without interruption for 11 s after the instant it is driven high under SYS-TEST-004.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): STK-SUP-015 asks for a simulator demonstration; the 11 s duration is an author proposal, and CON-SUP-108 is cited as the related input from which it is taken, not as an approved basis for it. The item is open until OP-SYS-029 is decided. Split from SYS-TEST-001 (F-sys-req-item-r2-032); reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-031 by a split into SYS-TEST-005, SYS-TEST-010, SYS-TEST-011, SYS-TEST-012 and SYS-TEST-013. This item observes only that the status signal stays high, which a fault or reset would interrupt (SYS-SAFE-002, SYS-SAFE-005, CON-SUP-109). An uninterrupted high level alone is not evidence that the supervised tasks, the control cycles or the watchdog refreshes run: a controller that drives the signal high and then stalls with the simulated watchdogs not enabled would also keep it high. Positive evidence is therefore observed in the same run and over the same 11 s: control-cycle progression (SYS-TEST-010), completion of every scheduled release of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG (SYS-TEST-011), window watchdog refreshes made while that watchdog is enabled (SYS-TEST-012) and independent watchdog refreshes made while that watchdog is enabled (SYS-TEST-013). The supervised-operation evidence counts only when SYS-TEST-005, SYS-TEST-006 and SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-013 all pass in that one run. The 11 s window is the full-pass bound of the run-time code check (CON-SUP-108, SYS-MEM-005); it is the author's proposal, not an input value, and needs confirmation (OP-SYS-029). Observation means for SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-013: OP-SYS-037.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005, the controller shall complete at least 1099 control cycles that each begin and end within the 11 s after the instant the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): the 11 s window and the count of 1099 control cycles are author proposals resting on an unapproved first-cycle assumption (OP-SYS-020 (a), OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-037); CON-SUP-101 is cited as the related input, not as an approved basis for the count. Open until these are decided. Split from SYS-TEST-005 (F-sys-req-item-r3-031): positive evidence of control-cycle progression over the interval in which SYS-TEST-005 observes the status signal high. The control cycle is the 10 ms period of CON-SUP-101. The count 1099 is the number of whole 10 ms control cycles that fit in 11 s when the first control cycle begins no later than 10 ms after the status signal is driven high; no input bounds that delay (OP-SYS-020 (a)), so the count needs confirmation (OP-SYS-037). The 11 s window: OP-SYS-029.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005, for each release that the default configuration schedules for T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT or T_DIAG in a control cycle beginning and ending within the 11 s after the instant the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004, the controller shall complete one execution of that task, released within that control cycle and begun no later than its configured start limit after that release, no later than the earlier of the expiry of its configured execution limit and the end of the period of that task, as defined in SYS-SUP-001, that follows the period containing that release.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): the 11 s window is an author proposal (OP-SYS-029); the cited constraints are the related inputs, not an approved basis for that value. Open until it is decided. Split from SYS-TEST-005 (F-sys-req-item-r3-031): positive evidence that all four supervised tasks execute over the interval in which SYS-TEST-005 observes the status signal high. The scheduled releases follow CON-SUP-101 (T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT every control cycle; T_DIAG in every tenth control cycle) and the execution limits follow CON-SUP-103 (SYS-CFG items). Together with the cycle count of SYS-TEST-010, a controller that releases no task, or stalls, fails this demonstration. Completion of a release scheduled near the end of the window may be observed after the window ends, up to its execution-limit expiry. Observation means: OP-SYS-037. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-076. The expected release slots are enumerated from the recorded control-cycle starts and the configured schedule (CON-SUP-101: T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT in every control cycle, T_DIAG in every tenth), not from the observed releases, so a slot without a release is not skipped.
