Each slot has finite failure criteria in order: no release of the task within its control cycle fails at the end of that cycle; no start within the configured start limit after the release fails at the expiry of that limit; no completion by the expiry of the configured execution limit fails at that expiry. The control cycle of the first T_DIAG release after start-up is open in OP-SYS-020 (b) and is taken from the configuration under test. The execution-limit expiry follows the measure decided in OP-SYS-013 (d). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-013. Finite outcome for a release that has begun but neither completes nor reaches its execution-limit expiry, which can occur if OP-SYS-013 (d) selects the task's processor time and the task is preempted without end: the slot fails at the end of the period of that task that follows the period of the release, if the release has not completed by then. That instant is consistent with the alive rule: it is the end of the alive window of SYS-SUP-001 that spans the period of the release and the following period, so the demonstration gives its verdict at the instant the alive rule can first judge two periods, and if no other release of the task completes in those two periods the controller declares an alive fault at the same instant, which SYS-TEST-006 also fails. If OP-SYS-013 (d) selects elapsed time, the execution-limit expiry (with the defaults at most 5 ms after release for a 10 ms task and 22 ms for T_DIAG) always comes first, and this criterion does not change the verdict. Every slot therefore has a verdict at a finite instant: the end of its control cycle for no release, the start-limit expiry for no start, and the earlier of the execution-limit expiry and the end of the following task period for no completion. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-012. The finite observation rule is now a criterion of the text: each scheduled release must complete by the earlier of its execution-limit expiry and the end of the task period that follows the period of the release. Applicability to each scheduled release: every release scheduled in the window lies in one period of its task under the configured schedule (SYS-SUP-001, SYS-CFG-001), and the following period of that task ends at a finite instant: at the end of the control cycle after the release cycle for T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, and 200 ms after the start of the release cycle for T_DIAG with the defaults. For a release scheduled near the end of the window this instant lies after the window, and the record continues until the verdict of the last slot, at most 200 ms after the start of the control cycle of the last T_DIAG release in the window. With elapsed time as the execution-time measure (OP-SYS-013 (d)) the execution-limit expiry always comes first and the added bound changes no verdict. With processor time, a release preempted without end never reaches its expiry, and a completion of another release of the task in the following period satisfies the alive rule (SYS-SUP-001, CON-SUP-102), so no input requires the preempted release to complete; the bound is then a completion expectation that the inputs do not state. It is an author proposal that needs approval, recorded in OP-SYS-047 (blocking); this item stays open until it is decided or OP-SYS-013 (d) selects elapsed time.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005, for each control cycle that begins and ends within the 11 s after the instant the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004, the controller shall make exactly one refresh of the simulated window watchdog while that watchdog is enabled, after the program-flow check of that control cycle has completed, no later than the largest delay after the end of that control cycle decided in OP-SYS-044, and at least 6 ms and at most 12 ms after the refresh made for the preceding control cycle, or, for the first control cycle after start-up, for which no earlier refresh exists, within the bounds relative to the reference instant that the first-refresh policy decided in OP-SYS-010 sets.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): the 11 s window is an author proposal (OP-SYS-029); the cited constraints are the related inputs, not an approved basis for that value. Open until it is decided. Split from SYS-TEST-005 (F-sys-req-item-r3-031): positive evidence of window watchdog refreshes over the interval in which SYS-TEST-005 observes the status signal high. Counting only refreshes made while the simulated watchdog is enabled rejects a controller that stalls with the watchdog not enabled. One refresh per control cycle at its end follows SYS-WDG-003 and CON-SUP-106; the 6 ms and 12 ms bounds are those of CON-SUP-106 (SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-078: refreshes are associated with eligible cycle ends. A refresh after the flow-check completion of cycle k and before the end of cycle k+1 is associated with cycle k; a cycle with no associated refresh or with two, and a refresh inside the window that is associated with no cycle, fail. The spacing is checked between the refreshes of consecutive cycles, 6 ms and 12 ms included (CON-SUP-106, SYS-WDG-002, SYS-WDG-006); for the first cycle after start-up the text and this verification apply the same rule (reworked for F-sys-req-set-r3-008): CON-SUP-106 defines the 6 ms to 12 ms window relative to a previous refresh, which the first refresh after start-up lacks, so the spacing check is not applied to it; its refresh is associated with its cycle as for every cycle, and its timing is checked against the reference instant and bounds of the first-refresh policy decided in OP-SYS-010, which may also exempt it. The verdict for the first cycle therefore depends on that decision and is pending until it is made; no policy is proposed here. The former minimum count of 1098 refreshes is removed; the number of cycles follows from the recorded cycle ends. The delay of each refresh after its cycle end is also recorded for SYS-WDG-008. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-063: the former bound 'before the end of the next control cycle' accepted a steady 9 ms delay. Each refresh must now lie no later than the OP-SYS-044 delay after the end of its own cycle (the same criterion as SYS-WDG-003 (V1) (v)); a refresh after the flow-check completion of cycle k and no later than that limit is associated with cycle k, and a refresh later than that limit fails. The spacing check of 6 ms to 12 ms is kept separately. The limit is undecided (OP-SYS-044, blocking).

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005, counting only refreshes of the simulated independent watchdog made while that watchdog is enabled, the controller shall make the first such refresh at or after the instant t0 at which the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004 less than 100 ms after t0, and each such refresh that follows a refresh made from t0 to t0 + 11 s, both included, less than 100 ms after that preceding refresh.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): the 11 s window is an author proposal (OP-SYS-029); the cited constraints are the related inputs, not an approved basis for that value. Open until it is decided. Split from SYS-TEST-005 (F-sys-req-item-r3-031): positive evidence of independent watchdog refreshes over the interval in which SYS-TEST-005 observes the status signal high. The 100 ms bound is the independent watchdog timeout of CON-SUP-106 (SYS-WDG-001, SYS-WDG-004). Counting only refreshes made while the simulated watchdog is enabled rejects a controller that stalls with the watchdog not enabled. Observation means: OP-SYS-037. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-079: the interval boundaries are explicit. Leading interval: from t0 to the first refresh at or after t0. Inter-refresh intervals: from each refresh made in the closed interval from t0 to t0 + 11 s to the next refresh, which may lie after t0 + 11 s, so the trailing interval is also bounded. Each interval must be shorter than 100 ms: a gap of exactly 100 ms fails, because SYS-WDG-004 requires refresh intervals shorter than the 100 ms timeout of CON-SUP-106.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005 and SYS-TEST-014, the controller shall declare no fault, as observed directly at the fault declarations on the simulated time base, from the instant the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004 until 11 s after that instant.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): STK-SUP-015 asks for simulator testability; the 11 s window is an author proposal, not an approved input value (OP-SYS-029), and the item is open until it is decided. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-071. The absence of a fault report on the serial line does not by itself show that no fault was declared: a report can start after the end of a serial capture, be cut off, or follow after a later service reply, and a positive control in another run does not show that supervision ran in this one. The verdict is therefore taken from the fault declarations observed directly on the simulated time base over the whole window (observation means open in OP-SYS-025 (c), OP-SYS-026 (b), OP-SYS-034 (a) and OP-SYS-037); a run in which the declaration record does not cover the whole window is not passed. Corroboration on the serial line in the same run: from the status edge until the first character of the GET STATUS request of SYS-TEST-014 (at least 11.02 s after the edge), the capture contains no occurrence of FLT followed by a comma, counted whether or not a line feed follows it, and a partial F, FL or FLT at the end of the capture counts as a report. A fault detected up to the end of the 11 s window has its report started, or completed, within 10 ms (SYS-DIAG-002; start or end of transmission per OP-SYS-007), and its first four characters take 0.35 ms at 115200 baud (CON-SUP-007), so its prefix lies inside the capture under either reading. The text below is the earlier rationale; where it differs, this paragraph applies. Split from SYS-TEST-001 (F-sys-req-item-r2-032); reworked for F-sys-req-item-r3-033 by a split into SYS-TEST-006, SYS-TEST-014 and SYS-TEST-015. The absence of a fault report is evidence of no fault declaration only when (1) supervision runs, (2) the serial path is observed, (3) a declared fault would reach the serial line inside the observed interval and (4) partial reports and resets cannot hide one. (1) Supervision runs: in the same run, SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-013 give positive evidence of control cycles, task completions and watchdog refreshes over the window, and SYS-TEST-015, on the same test build and configuration, shows that an alive fault injected at an instant from 100 ms to 11 s after the status signal goes high is declared and reported within 10 ms of the end of its alive window; the nominal run of SYS-TEST-005 must therefore use that test build with no hook activated. (2) Serial path: the capture of this run must also contain the start-up message of SYS-TEST-001 before the interval, and SYS-TEST-014 requires in this run an answer to GET STATUS sent just after the interval, so a stalled controller or an unconnected or unobserved serial path fails. (3) Detection: a fault declaration is detected by its fault report (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-002), transmitted within 10 ms of detection; the interval therefore extends 10 ms beyond the 11 s window of SYS-TEST-005 so that a fault detected up to the end of that window is still caught. It is also corroborated in the same run: a declared alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow or run-time code-integrity fault drives the status signal low within 50 ms (SYS-SAFE-002, observed by SYS-TEST-005) and alive, late-start, overrun and program-flow faults stop watchdog refreshes (SYS-WDG-005, SYS-WDG-007, observed by SYS-TEST-012 and SYS-TEST-013). (4) Partial reports and resets: the sequence FLT followed by a comma is counted wherever it occurs and whether or not the line is completed, so a report truncated after its fourth character fails this item. A report truncated before that needs a reset or a stall: any reset drives the status signal low (CON-SUP-109) and fails SYS-TEST-005, a software reset follows a fault report (CON-SUP-110), a watchdog-reset fault (code 8) is reported only after a reset, and a stall fails SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-014. No other defined output of the controller contains that sequence; the start-up message format (OP-SYS-002) and the STS state values (OP-SYS-001) are open, and the GET STATUS answer of SYS-TEST-014 lies after the interval. Window value: OP-SYS-029. Observation and injection means: OP-SYS-037, OP-SYS-038.

items.text: While the controller software runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and no fault injected, in the same run as SYS-TEST-005, when the verification environment sends the request GET STATUS on the simulated diagnostic serial line with its first character starting from 11.02 s to 11.1 s after the instant the status signal is driven high under SYS-TEST-004, the controller shall transmit on that line, within 50 ms of the end of the request, the complete answer STS,<state>,<fault count> of SYS-DIAG-007, with each field value and the end of the answer identified by the field and framing rules decided for SYS-DIAG-007 in OP-SYS-001.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): the 11 s window and the request interval from 11.02 s to 11.1 s are author proposals (OP-SYS-029); CON-SUP-113 gives the answer form and the 50 ms bound only. Open until decided. Split from SYS-TEST-006 (F-sys-req-item-r3-033): shows, in the run in which SYS-TEST-006 observes no fault report, that the controller still runs and that its transmissions on the simulated diagnostic serial line reach the verification environment at the end of the observed interval; together with the start-up message of SYS-TEST-001 captured before the interval, the serial path is shown observable on both sides of it. The request starts after the 11.01 s interval of SYS-TEST-006, so the answer cannot fall inside it, and it is sent after the 11 s window of SYS-TEST-005 and SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-013, so it does not change the normal-operation conditions those items observe (CON-SUP-114). Answer form and 50 ms bound per CON-SUP-113 (SYS-DIAG-007). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-080: the answer must contain both fields that CON-SUP-113 requires; their values are not judged because the state values and the meaning of the fault count are open (OP-SYS-001). No terminator is required: CON-SUP-112 specifies a line feed for FLT lines only, and the framing of service answers is open (OP-SYS-001); the approved framing is added to the criteria when it is decided. How a request is terminated is open (OP-SYS-001) and the measuring points of the 50 ms are open (OP-SYS-007); 'end of the request' is the end of transmission of its last character. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-064: the former criterion accepted an answer cut off after the first character of a field. The demonstration now requires the complete answer: STS, a comma, a <state> value of the approved form, a comma, a complete <fault count> value of the approved form and the approved end of the answer, all received within 50 ms of the end of the request; an answer whose end is not received by then, or whose fields are not complete under the approved rules, fails. CON-SUP-113 does not give the field forms or the framing; they are taken from the decision in OP-SYS-001 (blocking), and until then the criterion cannot be evaluated and the item stays open. The earlier statement that no terminator is required is withdrawn in favour of the approved framing.

items.text: When the test build of the controller software used in the run of SYS-TEST-005 runs on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, with the default configuration and the safe state not latched, and an alive fault for T_IN is injected through its fault-injection hook at one instant from 100 ms to 11 s after the instant the status signal is driven high in that run, so that alive supervision receives no completion of T_IN from the injection instant on while the releases, starts, executions, checkpoints and completions of T_IN seen by the timing and program-flow rules continue unchanged, as decided in OP-SYS-038, the controller shall complete the transmission of a fault report line with fault code 1 and entity T_IN on the simulated diagnostic serial line within 10 ms of the end of the alive window of T_IN determined under SYS-SUP-001 from the T_IN periods recorded in that run.
items.rationale: Derived proposal (F-sys-req-set-r1-010): STK-SUP-015 asks for simulator testability with fault injection; the injection range from 100 ms to 11 s is an author proposal (OP-SYS-029, OP-SYS-037), open until decided. Split from SYS-TEST-006 (F-sys-req-item-r3-033): positive control showing that, on the build and configuration of the nominal run, alive supervision is active inside the window of SYS-TEST-005 and that a declared fault reaches the simulated serial line. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-014 and F-sys-req-set-r1-082. (1) Deadline origin: the former 40 ms from the injection instant assumed that T_IN periods were already progressing at injection, which neither the 100 ms offset nor CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-102 establish (first-cycle alignment is open, OP-SYS-020). The run records on one time base the control-cycle starts that bound the T_IN periods (SYS-SUP-001), the completion of every T_IN execution, the injection instant, every fault declaration, every reset and the serial capture. The run qualifies only if at least one T_IN period boundary is recorded before the injection and T_IN period boundaries continue to be recorded after it; the end of the alive window E_a is then the end of the second consecutive T_IN period without a completed execution, taken from the record. The report deadline is 10 ms after E_a (CON-SUP-105, CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-002), with the end-of-transmission endpoint pending OP-SYS-007. (2) Validity against masking: stopping T_IN completion can also suppress its checkpoint or cause a timing fault, depending on the injected behaviour (OP-SYS-038) and on the checkpoint event (OP-SYS-021), so a program-flow, late-start or overrun fault can become detectable, and a reset follow (SYS-SUP-005, SYS-WDG-007), before E_a. The run is valid only if the record shows no fault of another class becoming detectable and no reset from the injection instant up to E_a; a run masked by an earlier fault or reset is invalid for the positive control and is neither passed nor failed. If no injected behaviour admitted under OP-SYS-038 gives a valid run, for example because the checkpoint of T_IN is signalled at completion (OP-SYS-021), the positive control is reported as not run, and SYS-TEST-006 lacks its positive control. (3) Pass: in a valid run exactly one alive declaration for T_IN is recorded at E_a, and a complete line FLT,1,T_IN,<ms since start> with its line feed is received no later than 10 ms after E_a; a valid run without that line by that instant fails. Repeating the run with injection instants near the start, middle and end of the window covers the whole window. Fault code 1 and entity per SYS-DIAG-003 and SYS-DIAG-004; hook per SYS-TEST-002. Activation of the hook, its injected behaviour and the time resolution of the recorded injection instant: OP-SYS-038; observation of cycles, completions and declarations: OP-SYS-037 and OP-SYS-034 (a). Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-012. A stimulus that stops T_IN itself from completing gives a competing fault in the first period: a release that does not start is late (SYS-SUP-002), one that starts and does not finish overruns at its execution-limit expiry (SYS-SUP-003), and one that is not released leaves its checkpoint missing (SYS-SUP-005, F-sys-req-set-r2-001). The positive control therefore uses a stimulus that acts on the input of the alive rule only: the hook withholds each T_IN completion from alive supervision, while the timing and flow rules still see T_IN start, execute, signal its checkpoint and complete within its limits. The run shows that alive supervision declares the fault when it receives no completion for two consecutive T_IN periods on the build and configuration of the nominal run; it does not show that a real stop of T_IN reaches alive supervision, which the verification of SYS-SUP-001 covers. This stimulus is an author proposal and needs approval (OP-SYS-038, now blocking). Positive-control criteria with this stimulus: a run is valid if the record shows T_IN completions continuing after the injection instant, no T_IN completion counted by alive supervision from the injection instant up to E_a, no fault of another class becoming detectable and no reset up to E_a; pass and fail are as in (3). The masking rule of (2) still applies, and the positive control is reported as not run only if OP-SYS-038 approves no isolating stimulus.

quality_waivers.rationale: The number 1 is the fault-code identifier of an alive fault defined in CON-SUP-112 (SYS-DIAG-003), not a physical quantity, so it carries no unit.

items.text: Test builds of the controller software shall provide a fault-injection hook for each of the alive, late-start, overrun, program-flow, start-up code-integrity, configuration-integrity, run-time code-integrity, watchdog-reset and configuration-range fault classes.
Builds of the controller software other than test builds shall contain no fault-injection hook.

open_points.text: Service interface not fully defined by CON-SUP-113: the allowed values of <state> in STS, what <fault count> counts (since power-on, since the latest reset, or entries in the history), the framing of the GET FAULTS answer (order, separator, end marker, answer when fewer than 8 reports are held), how a request is terminated, and the answer time for ERR. Affects SYS-DIAG-007, SYS-DIAG-008, SYS-DIAG-009, SYS-TEST-014 (complete STS answer, F-sys-req-set-r2-064).

Reset cause reporting: CON-SUP-111 requires a start-up message and that the reset cause is readable by the service tool, but gives no start-up message format, and CON-SUP-113 defines only GET STATUS and GET FAULTS and answers any other request with ERR, so no defined request returns the reset cause. A decision is needed on the message format and on the request (or STS field) that carries the cause. Affects SYS-RST-009, SYS-RST-010.
CON-SUP-112 defines the entity field only as a task name, CODE or CONFIG; no entity is given for fault code 8 (watchdog reset). Affects SYS-DIAG-004, SYS-RST-011.

Conflict between watchdog servicing and the fault reaction sequence: after a task fault the watchdogs are no longer refreshed (STK-SUP-005), and the window watchdog resets when not refreshed within 12 ms of its previous refresh (CON-SUP-106). That reset can occur before the fault report is transmitted (up to 10 ms, CON-SUP-112) and before the supervisor requests its software reset (up to 20 ms after safe-state entry, CON-SUP-110). The reset would then be classified as a window watchdog reset, not a supervisor reset, so the fault report can be lost and the three-consecutive-supervisor-reset latch of CON-SUP-110 might never be reached for task faults. A human decision is needed on the intended precedence. Affects SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-004, SYS-WDG-005, SYS-RST-001, SYS-RST-002, SYS-RST-004, SYS-DIAG-002.

Integrity criteria and the configuration producer/checker interface. For the program code image, CON-SUP-107 gives no integrity method, reference value, its storage location or how the build produces it. For the configuration block only the CRC-32 polynomial 0x04C11DB7 is given, not the initial value, the bit reflection of input and output or the final XOR; nor (F-sys-req-set-r1-005) the bytes the CRC covers (start and end of the covered range within the block), the serialization of multi-byte values (byte order, padding, field layout), the treatment of the stored CRC field (excluded from the covered range, or included so that the check compares against a fixed residue), or where the stored CRC is placed and in which byte order. A producer (the build tooling) and the checker can use the same polynomial and disagree on the result. A human decision is needed on these interface parameters, recorded with at least one reference valid block and its expected CRC value and reference invalid blocks (for example one bit changed inside the covered range and one bit changed in the stored CRC field), so that valid and invalid blocks for SYS-MEM-002, SYS-TEST-008 and SYS-TEST-009 can be produced reproducibly. These define the interface to the build tooling and must be decided before sys-arch fixes it. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision fixes which blocks pass the start-up configuration-integrity check and which integrity computation detects a run-time fault. Affects SYS-MEM-001, SYS-MEM-002, SYS-MEM-005, SYS-MEM-008, SYS-TEST-007, SYS-TEST-008, SYS-TEST-009.

CON-SUP-110 does not say whether a watchdog reset, an 'other' reset or a supervisor reset with a different fault code between supervisor resets with the same code breaks the 'consecutive' sequence, nor from which instant the 60 s of fault-free operation are counted. SYS-RST-004 covers only an uninterrupted sequence of same-code supervisor resets. Affects SYS-RST-004. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes when the safe state latches.

Diagnostic time references: whether 'sent within 10 ms of detection' (CON-SUP-112) means start or end of transmission (SYS-DIAG-002 takes the end), the start instant for <ms since start>, and from which event to which event the 50 ms service answer time of CON-SUP-113 is measured. Affects SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-DIAG-005, SYS-DIAG-007, SYS-DIAG-008. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes the timing verdicts of the fault report under CON-SUP-112, of the time stamp, and of the service answers under CON-SUP-113.

For a program-flow fault CON-SUP-112 requires a task name as entity but does not say which task is named (for example the task whose checkpoint is missing or out of order) nor what is reported when several checkpoints of one cycle are wrong. Affects SYS-SUP-005, SYS-DIAG-004. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes the content of program-flow fault reports.

Service requests in the safe state. Assessment of the available service time (F-sys-req-set-r2-009, recalculated for F-sys-req-set-r3-010), at 86.8 µs per character (115200 baud, 10 bit times per character: start bit, 8 data bits, stop bit, CON-SUP-007). Frame lengths: a fault report line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> with its line feed (CON-SUP-112) has 8 fixed characters (FLT, three commas, the one-digit code 1 to 9 and the line feed), plus the entity (4 characters for T_IN or CODE, 5 for T_OUT, 6 for T_CTRL, T_DIAG or CONFIG), plus 1 digit up to the largest width of <ms since start> open in OP-SYS-042 (d), taken here as 10 digits: 13 characters (1.13 ms) to 24 characters (2.08 ms). GET STATUS and GET FAULTS have 10 characters each (0.87 ms) before any terminator (OP-SYS-001); a request is complete only after its last character. Replies: ERR 3 characters (0.26 ms); STS,<state>,<fault count> at least 7 characters (0.61 ms) plus the fields and framing open in OP-SYS-001; GET FAULTS with 8 reports 104 to 192 characters (9.03 ms to 16.67 ms) before framing (OP-SYS-042). Reset request and reset event: after safe-state entry the controller transmits the fault report and then requests the software reset within 20 ms of entry (CON-SUP-110, SYS-RST-001, SYS-RST-013). Assumptions of this assessment: the fault report begins no earlier than safe-state entry, in the order CON-SUP-110 states, and its transmission ends with the stop bit of its line feed (end-of-transmission endpoint: OP-SYS-007); the reset request may follow that end with no added latency, which gives the earliest request; the reset event is the instant the requested software reset takes effect in the microcontroller and stops the USART transmission, observed on the simulator as the reset of the simulated core and USART in the simulator record; its latency after the request is a hardware fact of RM0486 that the inputs do not give, taken here as zero or more, so the earliest reset event is no earlier than the earliest request. The interruption verdict uses the reset event, not the reset request: a line is cut off when the reset event occurs before the stop bit of its last character. Results: (1) the earliest permitted reset request is 1.13 ms after entry (a 13-character report: entity T_IN or CODE and a one-digit time stamp) and the latest is 20 ms after entry, so no reply to a request completed after entry is guaranteed under the current set; (2) if the reset request is postponed to the full 20 ms and the reset event follows it with zero latency, the time left for a reply is 20 ms minus the time from entry to the end of the request, minus the fault report (1.13 ms to 2.08 ms) where it shares the line (OP-SYS-042); an ERR or STS reply fits only if the request ends at least the fault report time plus its reply time before 20 ms after entry, and a GET FAULTS reply of 8 reports fits only if the request ends no later than 1.25 ms (fault report and all 8 history entries of 24 characters) to 9.84 ms (all of 13 characters) after entry; a latency of the reset event after the request extends these limits by that latency; (3) a window-watchdog reset (OP-SYS-004, SYS-WDG-006) can end the interval before 20 ms, and a reset event during a reply cuts it off; (4) the 50 ms bound of CON-SUP-113 is therefore not met for every request completed after entry. A human decision is needed on: (a) whether a request completed after safe-state entry and before the reset is answered, discarded, or answered only when its whole reply fits before the reset request; (b) whether the reset request may be postponed within the 20 ms to complete a reply, and the order of fault report and reply; (c) the outcome for a request whose reply is cut off by the reset (no reply, partial reply, or a reply after the restart); (d) the same choice for a request completed before entry whose reply is still pending at entry; (e) whether requests are answered while the safe state is latched. Affects SYS-DIAG-007, SYS-DIAG-008, SYS-DIAG-009, SYS-RST-001, SYS-RST-013. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes which service requests are answered after safe-state entry and in the latched safe state.

Watchdog behaviour outside normal operation is not given: whether the watchdogs run during the start-up checks (if so, the start-up check of up to 1 MiB must complete before a timeout, and no start-up duration limit is given), and what happens in the latched safe state, where without refresh watchdog resets would recur at each timeout and each would report a watchdog-reset fault, against 'stay in the safe state' of STK-SUP-010. Whether a watchdog is active from reset is a hardware fact to be taken from RM0486 in the architecture, not assumed here. First refresh after start-up (F-sys-req-set-r3-008): CON-SUP-106 bounds a refresh relative to the previous refresh, and the first window-watchdog refresh after the watchdog is enabled has no previous refresh. Whether the hardware applies a window to that refresh relative to the enabling of the watchdog is a fact to be taken from RM0486, not assumed here. A decision is needed on the first-refresh policy: the reference instant and the bounds that the first refresh after start-up must meet, or that it is exempt from a spacing bound. Affects SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-004, SYS-WDG-008, SYS-RST-003, SYS-RST-004, SYS-TEST-007, SYS-TEST-008, SYS-TEST-009, SYS-TEST-012. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes watchdog behaviour during start-up and in the latched safe state, and the maximum start-up duration bounds the observation of SYS-TEST-007 to SYS-TEST-009.

CON-SUP-115 lists out-of-range configuration conditions in parentheses; whether the list is exhaustive, and the allowed ranges of other configuration values (for example a start limit relative to the period, or a checkpoint order naming tasks not in the task set), are not given. Affects SYS-CFG-008. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes which configuration data blocks latch the safe state.

CON-SUP-114 measures processor time 'at the configured core clock', but the core clock value is not given. Affects SYS-RES-001. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the processor-time verdict of SYS-RES-001 depends on the core clock.

Schedulability of the default configured schedule is not established. With the default execution limits (CON-SUP-103: 3 ms for each of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT; 20 ms for T_DIAG) and the task set of CON-SUP-101, application execution can reach 110 ms per 100 ms on the single processor (CON-SUP-001), and 9 ms of each 10 ms control cycle, before supervisor execution. No input gives workload evidence showing which execution times can occur together. To verify the configured schedule, a human decision or evidence is needed on: (a) worst-case execution time of each of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG, and which of them can coincide within one 10 ms control cycle and within one 100 ms frame; (b) worst-case supervisor execution per control cycle, including the run-time code check (at most 0.5 ms per cycle, CON-SUP-108), the end-of-cycle flow check and watchdog refresh, fault reporting and service-request handling (CON-SUP-114 bounds only the 1 s average in normal operation); (c) interrupt load from the time base and the diagnostic serial line; (d) the scheduling policy of the timer-driven scheduler (CON-SUP-006), including preemption and priorities, the release instant of T_CTRL and T_OUT relative to the cycle start for the 2 ms start limit, and whether the execution limit counts the task's own processor time or elapsed time from its start including preemption. Either the bounds show that the defaults fit, or the default limits change. The delay from the end of each control cycle to its window-watchdog refresh, whose cycle-to-cycle change SYS-WDG-008 limits to -4 ms to +2 ms (F-sys-req-set-r1-011), depends on (b), (c) and (d). Affects SYS-CFG-007, SYS-WDG-008; the decision can also affect SYS-CFG-005 and SYS-CFG-006.

CON-SUP-115 makes an unknown task a configuration fault but no input defines the approved set of supported task identifiers against which a task in the configuration data block is judged known or unknown. CON-SUP-101 names T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG as the supervised tasks, and STK-SUP-004 lets the configuration choose which tasks are supervised. A human decision is needed on (a) whether the approved set is exactly T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG or a different list, and (b) how that set is fixed independently of the configuration data block (for example as part of the program code image). Affects SYS-CFG-008.

No input states when a fault report enters the fault history relative to fault detection and to its transmission on the diagnostic serial line (CON-SUP-110, CON-SUP-112, CON-SUP-113). SYS-DIAG-010 takes entry before the transmission starts, so an interrupted transmission does not remove the report from the history. A human decision is needed to confirm this entry instant and to say whether a fault detected but not yet entered when a reset occurs (for example a window watchdog reset as in OP-SYS-004) must still appear in the history, and (c) the means by which the completion of a durable history entry is observed on the same time base as the diagnostic serial line in verification (SYS-DIAG-010, test T1, F-sys-req-set-r1-057). Affects SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-011, SYS-DIAG-010, SYS-DIAG-008. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes which reports the reset-surviving history holds.

Reset-flag interpretation for the classification required by CON-SUP-111 is not given in the inputs. Four points need an approved reference (RM0486 section and page, CON-SUP-002) or a human decision: (a) which reset flag or flags identify each of power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog and supervisor (software) reset; (b) which flags fall under 'other', for example an external pin reset or a supply-level reset, if the device has such flags, and whether any of them counts as power-on; (c) which class applies when more than one flag is set at start-up; (d) whether flags persist across later resets until software clears them, and if so when the controller clears them, so that each start-up classifies only the preceding reset. Without (a) to (c), the expected class for each flag pattern in the test of SYS-RST-008 cannot be fixed. Affects SYS-RST-008, SYS-RST-011, SYS-RST-007.

CON-SUP-105 lists the instant at which each fault becomes detectable (end of the alive window, expiry of a timing limit, end of the control cycle for flow, completion of the failing integrity computation) but gives none for the configuration-range fault of CON-SUP-115. The control-output reaction no longer needs it (SYS-SAFE-007, outputs low from reset per CON-SUP-109), and neither does the status-signal reaction (SYS-SAFE-008), but items that measure from the detection instant still do for this fault: the 10 ms fault report (SYS-DIAG-002), the <ms since start> field (SYS-DIAG-005) and the observation of SYS-TEST-009. A human decision is needed on the detectability instant of a configuration-range fault, for example completion of the range check of the configuration data block. Affects SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-DIAG-005, SYS-TEST-009. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision fixes the origin of the report deadline and time stamp of code 9.

Feasibility of holding both control outputs low from any reset (CON-SUP-109) is not established. CON-SUP-003 only makes GPIO available for the control outputs; no input states the external level of those pins before supervisor code can act. A feasibility analysis is needed, for each reset path that CON-SUP-111 distinguishes (power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor software reset, other, including any external pin or supply-level reset the device has), covering: (a) the pin state of the GPIO lines chosen for the two control outputs while the reset is asserted and from reset release until software first configures them, taken from RM0486 (CON-SUP-002) by section and page, not assumed; (b) whether any reset path leaves a pin driven at its level from before the reset, or leaves it undriven; (c) for any interval in which a pin is not driven low by the device, the board circuit (for example a pull-down at the pin or a default-off input on the actuator driver) that holds the external level low, which no input defines; (d) the longest interval from reset release to the instant software drives both outputs low, against any limit the human decision sets for it. In addition, CON-SUP-005 names only host tests and the Renode simulator; whether Renode models pin levels during reset is not given, so the hardware-held interval may need verification by analysis or on hardware instead of by test. A human decision or approved hardware evidence is needed. Affects SYS-SAFE-004.

Feasibility of holding the status signal low from any reset (CON-SUP-109) is not established. CON-SUP-003 only makes GPIO available for the status signal; no input states the external level of that pin before supervisor code can act. A feasibility analysis is needed, for each reset path that CON-SUP-111 distinguishes (power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor software reset, other, including any external pin or supply-level reset the device has), covering: (a) the pin state of the GPIO line chosen for the status signal while the reset is asserted and from reset release until software first configures it, taken from RM0486 (CON-SUP-002) by section and page, not assumed; (b) whether any reset path leaves the pin driven at its level from before the reset, which matters because the status signal is high in normal operation (SYS-SAFE-006) and resets such as a supervisor software reset or a watchdog reset can be taken from that state, or leaves it undriven; (c) for any interval in which the pin is not driven low by the device, the board circuit (for example a pull-down at the pin, or the input behaviour of the receiver of the status signal) that holds or makes the external level read as low, which no input defines; (d) the longest interval from reset release to the instant software drives the status signal low, against any limit the human decision sets for it. In addition, CON-SUP-005 names only host tests and the Renode simulator; whether Renode models pin levels during reset is not given, so the hardware-held interval may need verification by analysis or on hardware instead of by test. A human decision or approved hardware evidence is needed. Affects SYS-SAFE-005.

Alignment of the alive windows with start-up is not fully given. CON-SUP-102 starts alive supervision when the start-up checks pass and CON-SUP-105 counts the reaction from the end of the alive window; SYS-SUP-001 bounds each period by the starts of the control cycles in which the task's release is scheduled and counts from the first period that starts at or after the checks pass. The inputs do not state: (a) whether the first control cycle starts at the instant the start-up checks pass or at a later time-base tick, and the longest interval between the two; (b) in which control cycle after start-up the first release of T_DIAG (CON-SUP-101: every tenth control cycle) is scheduled, and how the configuration data block sets it. With (a) and (b) open, the latest instant at which a supervised task that never completes after start-up is detected is not bounded by the inputs: for T_DIAG it can be up to 9 control cycles later depending on (b). A human decision is needed to confirm the window alignment and to set these values or a limit on them. Affects SYS-SUP-001. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision bounds the latest alive detection after start-up.

No input defines the event that supplies a task checkpoint for the program-flow check of CON-SUP-104: at which point of a release's execution a supervised task signals its checkpoint (for example when it begins executing, at a configured point within its execution, or when it completes), and whether a task signals one checkpoint or more than one per release. SYS-SUP-005 assigns each checkpoint to the control cycle in which its task was released, following 'tasks released in that cycle' of CON-SUP-104. For T_DIAG this can conflict with CON-SUP-103: T_DIAG is released after T_OUT (CON-SUP-101), may start up to 2 ms after release and execute up to 20 ms, longer than the 10 ms control cycle, so a checkpoint signalled late in its execution can arrive after the end of its release cycle and be detected as a missing checkpoint although the release meets its timing limits. The same applies to any task whose release instant plus start limit plus execution limit extends past the end of its cycle; release instants are open in OP-SYS-013 (d). A human decision is needed on (a) the event that supplies each supervised task's checkpoint, (b) for a checkpoint that can arrive after the end of its release cycle, whether it is checked at the end of the release cycle, at the end of the cycle in which it arrives, or at the end of another configured cycle, and (c) whether the configuration data block sets these per task (STK-SUP-004). Affects SYS-SUP-005, SYS-CFG-004, SYS-TEST-015.

Fault history scope: CON-SUP-110 keeps the fault history across software and watchdog resets and loses it on power loss, but no input says whether a reset classified as 'other' by CON-SUP-111 (for example an external pin or supply-level reset, if the device has one) keeps or clears the history, and CON-SUP-113 ('the last 8 fault reports') does not say how faults detected at the same instant are ordered when that order decides which report is displaced. A human decision is needed on (a) the history content after each 'other' reset kind and (b) the order among faults detected at the same instant. Affects SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-011, SYS-DIAG-008. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes the history content after 'other' resets and which report is displaced.

CON-SUP-111 classifies the reset cause from the reset flags but does not say whether the flags alone are sufficient to tell a supervisor (software) reset from another software-requested reset or from a reset in the 'other' class, nor whether evidence besides the flags (for example a marker kept in the reset-surviving memory of CON-SUP-110) may or must corroborate the class. Flag meanings must come from RM0486 by section and page (CON-SUP-002) or from a human decision. A decision is needed on (a) whether flag-only classification separates all five classes and (b) if not, which additional evidence is permitted and how it combines with the flags. Related to OP-SYS-016. Affects SYS-RST-008.

Exit from the latched safe state: CON-SUP-110 keeps the latch across software and watchdog resets and loses it on power loss, and latches the safe state until a power-on reset; STK-SUP-010 ends it by a power cycle. No input says whether a reset classified as 'other' by CON-SUP-111 (for example an external pin or supply-level reset, if the device has one) keeps the latch, clears it as a power-on reset does, or is a permitted exit from the latched safe state. SYS-SAFE-010 holds the control outputs low until the next power-on reset, so a reset kind that clears the latch without being a power-on reset would end the latched safe state against that item. Which flags identify a power-on reset is OP-SYS-016. A human decision is needed on (a) the latch state after each 'other' reset kind and (b) whether any of them is a permitted exit from the latched safe state. Affects SYS-SAFE-010, SYS-SAFE-011, SYS-RST-003, SYS-RST-004, SYS-RST-005, SYS-RST-007. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes whether an 'other' reset ends the latched safe state.

No input gives a deadline from the expiry of a supervised task's start limit to the instant the controller declares the late-start fault. CON-SUP-103 gives a 100 µs measurement resolution, which fixes the granularity of the measured start delay but not when the comparison with the start limit is evaluated or the fault declared, and it does not say when a late start is detected. CON-SUP-105 makes the expiry of the timing limit the origin of the 50 ms safe-state reaction (SYS-SAFE-001, SYS-SAFE-002), so the detection latency is consumed inside that budget, which bounds the safety reaction without a separate detection deadline. A human decision is needed on (a) whether a separate detection deadline from the expiry of the start limit is required and, if so, its value, (b) the origin of that deadline: the expiry of the start limit (release plus configured start limit) or the first instant T_x at which the measured start delay exceeds the limit (SYS-SUP-002), which can lie up to one 100 µs measurement step after the expiry depending on OP-SYS-027 (F-sys-req-set-r1-064), and (c) the time base and precision with which the declaration instant is observed in verification, since the <ms since start> field of the fault report has millisecond resolution (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005). The former remark on SYS-SUP-003 is superseded by OP-SYS-026. Affects SYS-SUP-002, SYS-TEST-006. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision adds or omits a detection deadline and fixes its origin.

CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the execution limit expires, but no input approves a latency or tolerance between that expiry and the instant the controller declares the overrun fault, and an implementation cannot declare it at exactly the expiry instant. The 100 µs measurement resolution of CON-SUP-103 is the granularity of the measured execution time, not an approved detection latency; the former 100 µs bound of SYS-SUP-003 derived from it has been removed (this supersedes the remark on SYS-SUP-003 in OP-SYS-025). The expiry instant itself depends on the execution-time measure open in OP-SYS-013 (d). A human decision is needed on (a) the allowed detection latency from the expiry of the execution limit to the declaration of the overrun fault, and (b) the time base and resolution with which the declaration instant is observed in verification, since the <ms since start> field of the fault report has millisecond resolution only (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005). Affects SYS-SUP-003.

CON-SUP-103 gives a 100 µs measurement resolution for start delays and execution times but does not say how a true time that lies between two multiples of 100 µs is mapped to a measured value (truncation, rounding to nearest or rounding up), nor where the 100 µs steps are aligned relative to the release or the start of execution. With truncation, a start or execution up to 100 µs beyond the limit can be measured as equal to the limit and judged in time, although CON-SUP-103 defines a start later than the limit as a late start and an execution longer than the limit as an overrun. A human decision is needed on the mapping and alignment, so that the expected fault decision for true times within 100 µs above a limit can be fixed, and confirmation that a measured value lies less than one 100 µs step from the interval it measures, the tracking criterion used in SYS-SUP-004 and SYS-SUP-008 (F-sys-req-set-r1-065, F-sys-req-set-r1-067). Affects SYS-SUP-004, SYS-SUP-008, SYS-SUP-002, SYS-SUP-006, SYS-SUP-003, SYS-SUP-007. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes which releases are late starts or overruns under CON-SUP-103 and the mapping criteria of SYS-SUP-004 and SYS-SUP-008.

CON-SUP-103 makes the per-task start limits configuration values and gives a 100 µs measurement resolution, but no input says in which time unit a start limit is held in the configuration data block, nor whether only integer multiples of 100 µs are allowed. SYS-SUP-006 compares the measured start delay with the configured start limit without rounding either value, so the late-start decision is defined for either answer; the decision changes which limit values the configuration may hold and whether the configuration range check (SYS-CFG-008, CON-SUP-115) rejects a limit that is not a multiple of 100 µs. A human decision is needed on the unit and the allowed granularity of configured start limits. Affects SYS-SUP-006, SYS-SUP-002, SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-008, SYS-WDG-007. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes which configured start limits the range check accepts.

STK-SUP-015, CON-SUP-005 and CON-SUP-116 require simulator-based verification but give no duration of fault-free operation that demonstrates the controller running supervised control cycles on the Renode simulator. SYS-TEST-005 and SYS-TEST-006 use 11 s, the full-pass bound of the run-time code check (CON-SUP-108); this value is an author proposal, not an input. Because the first control cycle may start later than the instant the status signal goes high (OP-SYS-020 (a)), the 11 s window may end shortly before the first full pass completes. A human decision is needed to confirm or replace the demonstration duration. Affects SYS-TEST-005, SYS-TEST-006, SYS-TEST-010, SYS-TEST-011, SYS-TEST-012, SYS-TEST-013, SYS-TEST-014, SYS-TEST-015. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the demonstration windows of SYS-TEST-005, SYS-TEST-006 and SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-015 rest on this unapproved value; these items are marked derived and open (F-sys-req-set-r1-010).

The valid-start verification of SYS-MEM-004 must observe, on one time base, when each of the three start-up checks completes and when the first application task is released, so that their order can be compared. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, and no input states how the completion of each start-up check, or the release of an application task, is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator. A decision is needed on the observation means (for example a test-build event record or simulator execution trace at points that the architecture identifies) and on its time resolution. Affects SYS-MEM-004, SYS-TEST-004, SYS-TEST-007, SYS-TEST-008. Non-blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): this point concerns the means of observation in verification; it does not change a required outcome or a pass criterion. Reviewed for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: deferrable to the system qualification specification, because the choice of observation means decides neither whether a required demonstration can be run nor its outcome.

The verification of SYS-MEM-005 must observe, on one time base, the start of each control cycle and the completion of each successful full pass of the run-time code integrity check. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, the fault report of SYS-DIAG-002 reports faults and not pass completions, and no input states how a pass completion or a control-cycle start is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator. A decision is needed on the observation means (for example a test-build event record or simulator execution trace at points that the architecture identifies) and on its time resolution. Related to OP-SYS-030, which covers the start-up check completions of SYS-MEM-004. Affects SYS-MEM-005. Non-blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): this point concerns the means of observation in verification; it does not change a required outcome or a pass criterion. Reviewed for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: deferrable to the system qualification specification, because the choice of observation means decides neither whether a required demonstration can be run nor its outcome.

The verification of SYS-MEM-008 must observe, for every control cycle and on the same time base as the control-cycle starts of OP-SYS-031, the start address and end address of every image range that the run-time code integrity check processes in that cycle. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, and no input states how the processed range is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator. A decision is needed on the observation means (for example a test-build event record or simulator memory-access trace at points that the architecture identifies). Related to OP-SYS-031. Affects SYS-MEM-008, SYS-MEM-005. Non-blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): this point concerns the means of observation in verification; it does not change a required outcome or a pass criterion. Reviewed for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: deferrable to the system qualification specification, because the choice of observation means decides neither whether a required demonstration can be run nor its outcome.

Second fault before the reset. SYS-RST-002 defines the safe-state entry instant of each fault, and SYS-RST-001 counts the 20 ms reset deadline from the entry instant of the first fault after the latest reset (F-sys-req-set-r1-008). CON-SUP-110 does not say how a fault detected after safe-state entry and before the software reset request is handled: (a) whether its fault report must also be transmitted before the reset request (SYS-RST-013), and (b) whether the later fault moves the 20 ms reset deadline to its own entry instant or the deadline stays with the first fault, since a report of the later fault may not fit before the deadline of the first. (c) which fault code is attributed to the supervisor reset that follows when faults with different codes are detected before it, which decides the count of CON-SUP-110 at the next start-up (F-sys-req-set-r2-004); SYS-RST-004 takes the code of the fault whose safe-state entry started the reset deadline, read from the order of CON-SUP-110, and needs confirmation. A human decision is needed on (a), (b) and (c). Affects SYS-RST-001, SYS-RST-002, SYS-RST-004, SYS-RST-013, SYS-DIAG-002. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the decision changes the reaction sequence and the reset deadline after a second fault.

The verification of SYS-SAFE-003 must record, on one common time base, the rule-defined fault event of CON-SUP-105 (end of the alive window, expiry of a timing limit, end of the control cycle for flow, completion of the failing integrity computation), every level change of the two control outputs and the next reset, with a resolution that orders an output transition close to the event; the millisecond <ms since start> field of the fault report (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005) cannot do this. It must also set each control output high or low before the event and request a low output high after it. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, and no input states (a) how the rule-defined fault event is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator, (b) the common time base and its resolution, or (c) which part drives the control outputs in normal operation and how a test build sets their levels or requests them high. A decision is needed on the observation and control means (for example a test-build event record or simulator execution trace at points that the architecture identifies). Related to OP-SYS-030, OP-SYS-031, OP-SYS-025 and OP-SYS-026. Affects SYS-SAFE-003, SYS-TEST-006, SYS-TEST-015. Non-blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): this point concerns the means of observation in verification; it does not change a required outcome or a pass criterion. Reviewed for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: deferrable to the system qualification specification, because the choice of observation means decides neither whether a required demonstration can be run nor its outcome.

The verification of SYS-SAFE-009 must record, on one common time base, the rule-defined fault event of CON-SUP-105 (end of the alive window, expiry of a timing limit, end of the control cycle for flow, completion of the failing integrity computation), every level change of the status signal and the next reset, with a resolution that orders a status-signal transition close to the event; the millisecond <ms since start> field of the fault report (CON-SUP-112, SYS-DIAG-005) cannot do this. It must also exercise the hold with the status signal already low at the event and request it high after the event. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, and no input states (a) how the rule-defined fault event is made observable in a test build or on the Renode simulator, (b) the common time base and its resolution, or (c) how a test build sets the status signal low before the event while the start-up checks have passed, since SYS-SAFE-006 drives it high in normal operation, and how it requests the signal high after the event. A decision is needed on the observation and control means; the same means as for OP-SYS-034 may serve. Related to OP-SYS-034. Affects SYS-SAFE-009. Non-blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): this point concerns the means of observation in verification; it does not change a required outcome or a pass criterion. Reviewed for F-sys-req-set-r2-011: deferrable to the system qualification specification, because the choice of observation means decides neither whether a required demonstration can be run nor its outcome.

Precedence between checkpoint receipt and the end-of-cycle program-flow evaluation when they coincide. CON-SUP-104 checks program flow once per control cycle at its end, and CON-SUP-105 makes the end of the control cycle the detection instant of a flow fault, but no input says whether a checkpoint received by the supervisor at the same instant as the end of its assigned control cycle has arrived for that cycle (receipt precedes evaluation) or has not arrived (evaluation precedes receipt). The choice decides whether a program-flow fault (code 4, CON-SUP-112) is declared for that cycle. A human decision is needed on (a) the precedence rule for a coincident receipt, and (b) how coincidence is defined and produced in verification: the time base and resolution at which the receipt instant and the end of the control cycle are compared (for example whether the 100 µs resolution of CON-SUP-103 applies to checkpoints), and how a test build or the Renode simulator places a receipt at the instant of the end of a cycle. SYS-SUP-005 fixes the cases strictly before and strictly after the end only. Related to OP-SYS-021 and OP-SYS-034. Affects SYS-SUP-005, SYS-SUP-009.

The supervised-operation demonstration of SYS-TEST-010 to SYS-TEST-013 must observe on the Renode simulator, on one time base with the status signal of SYS-TEST-005, the beginning and end of each control cycle, the release and completion of each execution of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG, each refresh of the simulated window watchdog and of the simulated independent watchdog, whether each simulated watchdog is enabled, and every fault declaration (SYS-TEST-006). CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 provide fault-injection hooks only, and no input states how these events are made observable in a test build or on the simulator. A decision is needed on the observation means (for example a test-build event record, or simulator execution and peripheral-access traces at points that the architecture identifies) and its time resolution. In addition, the minimum count of 1099 control cycles (SYS-TEST-010) assumes that the first control cycle begins no later than 10 ms after the status signal is driven high (the former count of 1098 window-watchdog refreshes of SYS-TEST-012 is replaced by a per-cycle association, F-sys-req-set-r1-078); no input bounds that delay (OP-SYS-020 (a)), and the 11 s window is itself an author proposal (OP-SYS-029). A human decision is needed to confirm or replace this count. Related to OP-SYS-031. The observation means also serve the verification of SYS-CFG-009 and SYS-WDG-006, whose required outcomes they do not change. Affects SYS-TEST-006, SYS-TEST-010, SYS-TEST-011, SYS-TEST-012, SYS-TEST-013, SYS-TEST-015. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r1-013): the minimum count of SYS-TEST-010 is an unapproved proposal; the observation-means part alone would not block.

The positive-control run of SYS-TEST-015 must activate the alive fault-injection hook for T_IN at a chosen instant inside the window of SYS-TEST-005 and record that instant on one time base with the status signal and the capture of the simulated diagnostic serial line. CON-SUP-116 and SYS-TEST-002 require the hooks to exist in test builds but no input states how the verification environment activates a hook during a run on the Renode simulator, what the injected alive fault does to T_IN (SYS-TEST-015 assumes that no execution of T_IN completes from the injection instant on), or the time resolution of the recorded injection instant. A decision is needed on the activation means, the injected behaviour and the resolution; the same means as for OP-SYS-037 may serve. Whether the injected behaviour stops only the completion of T_IN, or also its checkpoint or its timing, decides whether a valid run without an earlier competing fault can be produced (SYS-TEST-015, F-sys-req-set-r1-014). Affects SYS-TEST-015, SYS-TEST-006, SYS-WDG-003 (V2, F-sys-req-set-r3-014). Isolating stimulus proposed in SYS-TEST-015 (F-sys-req-set-r2-012): the alive hook withholds from alive supervision only each completion of T_IN from the injection instant on, while the releases, starts, executions, checkpoints and completions of T_IN seen by the timing and program-flow rules continue unchanged, so no late-start, overrun or program-flow fault is caused. A human decision is needed to approve this stimulus, or another that isolates alive supervision, as the positive control. The only other stimulus that avoids a competing fault, a T_IN release that starts, signals its checkpoint and is then preempted without end, works only if OP-SYS-013 (d) selects the task's processor time and OP-SYS-021 places the checkpoint before completion. Blocking (F-sys-req-set-r2-011; marked non-blocking earlier under F-sys-req-set-r1-013): without an approved isolating stimulus no valid run of SYS-TEST-015 exists, and SYS-TEST-006 has no positive control. The activation means and the time resolution of the recorded injection instant are observation choices that can be deferred to the system qualification specification.

Release order as a configuration value (F-sys-req-set-r1-001). CON-SUP-101 releases T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT in that order every 10 ms, and STK-SUP-004 requires the order of the supervised tasks to be set by configuration. SYS-CFG-001 takes the checkpoint order from the configuration data block; no input says whether the release order is also a configuration value or is fixed by the timer-driven scheduler (CON-SUP-006), nor whether a configuration may set a release order that differs from the checkpoint order. A human decision is needed on (a) where the release order is held and (b) whether it must equal the checkpoint order. Blocking: the decision changes the content of SYS-CFG-001 and of the configuration range check. Affects SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-004, SYS-CFG-008, SYS-CFG-009.

Validity and precedence of the start-up checks when an integrity failure and a range violation can both be observed (F-sys-req-set-r1-002). SYS-RST-012 requires a software reset after a configuration-integrity fault (code 6), and SYS-RST-003 latches the safe state after a configuration-range fault (code 9) (CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-115). When the stored CRC-32 of the configuration data block does not match its content, the values in the block are not known to be the configured values, yet the range check of SYS-CFG-008 can still find a value out of range in them, possibly before the CRC comparison has completed. No input says: (a) whether a range check of a block whose integrity check has failed, or has not yet completed, is valid; (b) which outcome applies when both checks fail: software reset with code 6, latch with code 9, or another outcome; (c) which fault reports are transmitted and entered in the fault history in that case, and in which order; (d) whether the range check may run before the integrity check has completed; (e) whether either configuration check is valid when the start-up code-integrity check has failed (code 5). A human decision is needed on (a) to (e). Blocking: the decision selects between a recoverable reset and a latch until power-on for the same block. Affects SYS-MEM-002, SYS-CFG-008, SYS-RST-003, SYS-RST-012, SYS-RST-014, SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-TEST-008, SYS-TEST-009.

Active functions when the start-up checks pass while the safe state is latched (F-sys-req-set-r1-003). After a latch under SYS-RST-003 or SYS-RST-004 and a later software or watchdog reset, the start-up checks can pass again (CON-SUP-107) while SYS-SAFE-010 and SYS-SAFE-011 keep the control outputs and the status signal low until a power-on reset (CON-SUP-110). No input says whether, in that state: (a) application tasks are released (SYS-MEM-004 gives only the release gate); (b) alive, timing and program-flow supervision run (CON-SUP-102 starts alive supervision when the start-up checks have passed, SYS-SUP-001); if tasks are not released while alive supervision runs, an alive fault is detected in every alive window; (c) the run-time code integrity check runs (SYS-MEM-005, SYS-MEM-008); (d) faults detected in that state are reported, entered in the fault history and followed by a software reset (SYS-RST-001 and SYS-RST-002 apply only while the safe state is not latched); (e) the watchdogs are refreshed (related to OP-SYS-010); (f) service requests are answered (related to OP-SYS-009). A human decision is needed on the functions active in this state under CON-SUP-110; the entry conditions of SYS-SUP-001, SYS-MEM-005, SYS-MEM-008 and the watchdog items are then aligned with it. Blocking. Affects SYS-RST-003, SYS-RST-004, SYS-SUP-001, SYS-MEM-005, SYS-MEM-008, SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-004, SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-SAFE-010, SYS-SAFE-011.

Concurrent traffic on the diagnostic serial line (F-sys-req-set-r1-004). The start-up message (SYS-RST-009, CON-SUP-111), fault reports (SYS-DIAG-002, CON-SUP-112) and service replies (SYS-DIAG-007 to SYS-DIAG-009, CON-SUP-113) share the one 115200 baud line of CON-SUP-007, and requests can arrive on it at any time. No input says how a fault report that becomes due is handled while another line is being transmitted, or when several fault reports are pending at once. At 86.8 µs per character (10 bit times), a fault report of 8 fixed characters plus the entity (4 to 6 characters) plus the digits of <ms since start> takes from 1.13 ms (13 characters: 4-character entity, 1 digit) to 2.08 ms (24 characters: 6-character entity, 10 digits) (recalculated for F-sys-req-set-r3-010), and a GET FAULTS answer of 8 such reports takes up to 16.7 ms before any framing (OP-SYS-001), longer than the 10 ms report deadline; at most 4 reports of 24 characters fit back to back in 10 ms. A human decision is needed on: (a) which traffic may be in progress or pending together (start-up message, fault reports, service replies, received requests); (b) the frame-handling rule when a fault report becomes due during another transmission: wait for the end of the current line, abort it, or interleave at line boundaries, and whether an aborted reply is resent or marked; (c) the order of several pending fault reports and the largest number that must meet the 10 ms deadline together; (d) the largest width of <ms since start> and the start-up message length, so that the admitted lengths can be checked against the 10 ms report deadline and the 50 ms answer deadline; (e) whether a service-answer deadline of CON-SUP-113 may be exceeded when fault reports take precedence. OP-SYS-033 covers only a later fault near the software reset. Blocking: these rules decide whether SYS-DIAG-002 and SYS-DIAG-007 to SYS-DIAG-009 can be met together. Affects SYS-DIAG-002, SYS-DIAG-007, SYS-DIAG-008, SYS-DIAG-009, SYS-RST-009, SYS-RST-013.

Platform and simulator dependencies for reset-surviving state (F-sys-req-set-r1-012). SYS-RST-004 to SYS-RST-007 and SYS-DIAG-010 rely on state that survives software and watchdog resets but not power loss (CON-SUP-110): the safe-state latch (SYS-RST-005), the fault history (SYS-RST-006, SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-011) and the reset-sequence state from which SYS-RST-004 counts consecutive same-code supervisor resets and the 60 s of fault-free operation (held separately or derived from the history, a design choice). The inputs do not establish: (a) which memory of the STM32N657X0 keeps its content through a software reset, an independent-watchdog reset and a window-watchdog reset, and loses it, or can be recognised as invalid, after power loss, to be cited from RM0486 by section and page (CON-SUP-002); (b) that the start-up code leaves that memory uninitialised on these resets; (c) whether the Renode STM32N6 platform description (CON-SUP-005) preserves that memory through each modelled reset kind and clears it on a modelled power-on reset; (d) whether a reset that occurs while the latch, the history or the reset-sequence state is being updated leaves a usable record, and if not what the controller does at the next start-up (the inputs give no integrity or validity rule for this memory); (e) the content after an 'other' reset (OP-SYS-022, OP-SYS-024). Evidence method proposed for each property, pending decision: (a) analysis against RM0486; (b) inspection of the start-up code and memory placement, supported by test on the simulator; (c) test on the Renode simulator injecting each reset kind and reading back the retained values, plus an analysis of the simulator model against RM0486 because simulator fidelity is not given; if the model does not preserve the memory, verification on hardware or by analysis is needed (CON-SUP-005 does not require hardware); (d) analysis of every update sequence for the state reached after a reset between any two write steps, supported by simulator tests that inject a reset at each step (CON-SUP-116). A human decision is needed on (d) and on accepting these evidence methods; (a) to (c) need approved hardware and simulator evidence. Blocking: without them the retention obligations of CON-SUP-110 are not shown feasible on the selected platform. Affects SYS-RST-004, SYS-RST-005, SYS-RST-006, SYS-RST-007, SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-010, SYS-DIAG-011.

Largest delay from the end of a control cycle to its window-watchdog refresh (F-sys-req-set-r2-063, F-sys-req-set-r2-067). CON-SUP-106 requires one refresh per control cycle at its end and limits only the spacing between refreshes to 6 ms to 12 ms; CON-SUP-104 places the program-flow check, which precedes the refresh (SYS-WDG-003), at the same end. No input gives the largest delay after the end of the cycle at which a refresh still counts as made at its end, so a steady delay of up to 9 ms meets the spacing check and SYS-WDG-008. A human decision is needed on that delay and on the instant it is measured to (the refresh as recorded on the simulator time base). The smallest feasible value depends on the supervisor work before the refresh (OP-SYS-013 (b), (c), (d)). Affects SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-008, SYS-TEST-012. Blocking: the decision sets a pass criterion of SYS-WDG-003 (V1) and of SYS-TEST-012.

Latest window-watchdog reset instant when refreshes stop (F-sys-req-set-r2-008). CON-SUP-106 makes a refresh later than 12 ms after the previous one invalid, and a refresh at exactly 12 ms is accepted (SYS-WDG-006, W1), but no input gives a tolerance between the 12 ms limit and the reset when no refresh follows. The window watchdog counts in discrete steps set by its clock and prescaler (to be cited from RM0486 by section and page in the design, CON-SUP-002), so the reset occurs at an instant after 12 ms that the inputs do not bound. A human decision is needed on the latest admitted reset instant after the previous refresh (12 ms plus an approved tolerance), used as the one criterion in SYS-WDG-006 (W2), SYS-WDG-003 (V4), SYS-WDG-007 and SYS-SUP-009, and on whether the simulator model of the window watchdog is accepted as evidence for it (OP-SYS-037). Affects SYS-WDG-006, SYS-WDG-003, SYS-WDG-007, SYS-SUP-009. Blocking: the decision sets the pass criterion of the no-refresh case.

Configured task periods and the application release schedule (F-sys-req-set-r3-001). SYS-CFG-001 takes the period of each supervised task from the configuration data block (STK-SUP-004), and SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-005 judge alive and program flow against the configured schedule defined in SYS-CFG-001. CON-SUP-006 states that the timer-driven scheduler runs the cyclic tasks at 10 ms and 100 ms periods, and CON-SUP-101 gives the default schedule. No input says whether a configured period that differs from these defaults changes the application releases or only the supervision. A human decision is needed on: (a) whether the timer-driven scheduler takes the release period of each supervised task from the configuration data block, or keeps its own periods with the configured periods used only for supervision; (b) the supported periods (only 10 ms and 100 ms, every integer multiple of the 10 ms control cycle, or another set), and whether a period outside that set is a configuration-range fault in addition to those of CON-SUP-115 (see OP-SYS-011); (c) if the scheduler keeps its own periods, whether a configured period that differs from the period at which the scheduler releases that task is rejected at start-up. Blocking: the decision sets whether changing a configured period changes the releases that SYS-SUP-001 and SYS-SUP-005 check, and the content of SYS-CFG-001 and of the configuration range check. Affects SYS-CFG-001, SYS-CFG-008, SYS-CFG-009, SYS-SUP-001, SYS-SUP-005, SYS-TEST-011.

Completion bound added by SYS-TEST-011 (F-sys-req-set-r3-012). SYS-TEST-011 requires each release scheduled in its window to complete no later than the earlier of its execution-limit expiry and the end of the task period that follows the period of the release, so that every release slot has a verdict at a finite instant. If OP-SYS-013 (d) selects elapsed time as the execution-time measure, the expiry always comes first and the bound changes no verdict. If it selects the task's processor time, a release preempted without end never reaches its expiry: CON-SUP-103 then gives no overrun, and CON-SUP-102 gives no alive fault while another release of the task completes in each pair of consecutive periods, so no input requires that release to complete. A human decision is needed to approve this completion bound as a verification criterion of the fault-free demonstration, to set another finite rule, or to decide that a release not completed at the end of the observation is reported without a verdict. Blocking: the decision sets a pass criterion of SYS-TEST-011; it no longer needs a decision if OP-SYS-013 (d) selects elapsed time. Affects SYS-TEST-011.
